1.115.m: Gold, gems, pearls, and silver as well, O Acyuta, / and diverse priestly gifts here, and whatever else is precious,

1.115.s:
ātmānaṃ bhāskaraṃ matvā yajñaṃ tasmai nivedayet .
tattadavyaktarūpāya bhāskarāya nivedayet . . 37
1.115.d:
आत्मानं भास्करं मत्वा यज्ञं तस्मै निवेदयेत् ।
तत्तदव्यक्तरूपाय भास्कराय निवेदयेत् ॥ 37
1.115.m: he should offer as a sacrifice to him, regarding himself as the Sun; / he should offer all that to the Sun whose form is unmanifest.

1.115.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe ādityamāhātmye sūryapūjāvidhivarṇanaṃ
nāma pañcadaśādhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . 115 .
ravipūjāvidhivarṇanam
1.115.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे आदित्यमाहात्म्ये सूर्यपूजाविधिवर्णनं
नाम पञ्चदशाधिकशततमोऽध्यायः । 115 ।
रविपूजाविधिवर्णनम्
1.115.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and fifteenth chapter, named 'Description of the Procedure for Sun Worship', in the discourse on the Greatness of Āditya, in the Seventh-Day Rite of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Procedure for Sun Worship

1.116.s:
brahmovāca
kṛṣṇa rājā mahānāsīdyayātikulasambhavaḥ .
satrājiditi vikhyātaścakravartī mahābalaḥ . . 1
1.116.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
कृष्ण राजा महानासीद्ययातिकुलसम्भवः ।
सत्राजिदिति विख्यातश्चक्रवर्ती महाबलः ॥ 1
1.116.m: Brahmā said: / O Kṛṣṇa, there was a great king born in the lineage of Yayāti, / renowned as Satrājit, an emperor of great might.

1.116.s:
prabhāvaistejasā kāntyā kṣāntyā balasamanvitaḥ .
dhairyagambhīryasampanno vadānyo yaśasānvitaḥ . . 2
1.116.d:
प्रभावैस्तेजसा कान्त्या क्षान्त्या बलसमन्वितः ।
धैर्यगम्भीर्यसम्पन्नो वदान्यो यशसान्वितः ॥ 2
1.116.m: Endowed with power, splendour, beauty, forbearance, and strength, / full of steadfastness and depth, generous, endowed with renown,

1.116.s:
buddhyā vikramadakṣaśca sampanno brāhmaṇāyataḥ .
kṛtī kavistathā śūraḥ ṣaṭpadākhyairna nirjitaḥ . . 3
1.116.d:
बुद्ध्या विक्रमदक्षश्च सम्पन्नो ब्राह्मणायतः ।
कृती कविस्तथा शूरः षट्पदाख्यैर्न निर्जितः ॥ 3
1.116.m: skilled in valour through his intellect, accomplished, dedicated to brahmins, / skilled, wise, and brave, undefeated by the six enemies,

1.116.s:
sadā pañcasu raktaśca vasumadbhirna nirjitaḥ .
rudratā vasubhirjātaiḥ sattvaśraddhāsamanvitaḥ . . 4
1.116.d:
सदा पञ्चसु रक्तश्च वसुमद्भिर्न निर्जितः ।
रुद्रता वसुभिर्जातैः सत्त्वश्रद्धासमन्वितः ॥ 4
1.116.m: ever devoted to the five, not overcome by those who possess wealth, / formidable as Rudra with the Vasus who arose, endowed with goodness and faith,

1.116.s:
ambujasyāṇḍajasyeva ātreyasya tathācyuta .
ambujāyāstathā kṛṣṇa vāryapātraṃ sa vai vibho . . 5
1.116.d:
अम्बुजस्याण्डजस्येव आत्रेयस्य तथाच्युत ।
अम्बुजायास्तथा कृष्ण वार्यपात्रं स वै विभो ॥ 5
1.116.m: just like the lotus-born [Brahmā], the egg-born [Garuḍa], or the descendant of Atri [the Moon], O Acyuta, / and like the lotus-born [Lakṣmī], O Kṛṣṇa, he was indeed an ocean of virtues, O lord.

1.116.s:
gāṅgeyena bale tulyaḥ paulastyārcāśramo yathā .
gāṅgeyasya tathā kṛṣṇa dhiṣaṇasya hareryathā . . 6
1.116.d:
गाङ्गेयेन बले तुल्यः पौलस्त्यार्चाश्रमो यथा ।
गाङ्गेयस्य तथा कृष्ण धिषणस्य हरेर्यथा ॥ 6
1.116.m: In strength he was equal to the son of Gaṅgā [Bhīṣma]; like the ascetic striving in worship of Pulastya's descendant [Rāvaṇa], / so was he to the son of Gaṅgā, O Kṛṣṇa, and like Bṛhaspati to Hari.

1.116.s:
kāmyaśca dvijabhaktastu tathā vālmīkivatsadā .
vyāsasya devaśārdūla jāmadagnyasya vā vibhoḥ . . 7
1.116.d:
काम्यश्च द्विजभक्तस्तु तथा वाल्मीकिवत्सदा ।
व्यासस्य देवशार्दूल जामदग्न्यस्य वा विभोः ॥ 7
1.116.m: Desirable and devoted to twice-born [brahmins], ever like Vālmīki, / like Vyāsa, O tiger among gods, or like the mighty son of Jamadagni [Paraśurāma],

1.116.s:
eṣāṃ naikairguṇairyuktaḥ sa rājā kṣmātale vibho .
śaśāsa sa mahābāhuḥ saptadvīpāṃ vasundharām . . 8
1.116.d:
एषां नैकैर्गुणैर्युक्तः स राजा क्ष्मातले विभो ।
शशास स महाबाहुः सप्तद्वीपां वसुन्धराम् ॥ 8
1.116.m: endowed with the many virtues of these [illustrious figures], O lord, that mighty-armed king / ruled upon the surface of the earth over the land of seven continents,

1.116.s:
yasmingāthāṃ pragāyanti ye purāṇavido janāḥ .
satrājite mahābāhau kṛṣṇa dhātrīṃ samāśrite . . 9
1.116.d:
यस्मिन्गाथां प्रगायन्ति ये पुराणविदो जनाः ।
सत्राजिते महाबाहौ कृष्ण धात्रीं समाश्रिते ॥ 9
1.116.m: about whom people knowing the Purāṇas sing a song / when the mighty-armed Satrājit, O Kṛṣṇa, held sway over the earth:

1.116.s:
yāvatsūrya udeti sma yāvacca pratitiṣṭhati .
satrājitaṃ tu tatsarvaṃ kṣetramityamidhīyate . . 1.116.10
1.116.d:
यावत्सूर्य उदेति स्म यावच्च प्रतितिष्ठति ।
सत्राजितं तु तत्सर्वं क्षेत्रमित्यमिधीयते ॥ 1.116.10
1.116.m: 'As far as the sun rises and as far as it sets, / all of that is declared to be the domain of Satrājit.'

1.116.s:
sa sarvaratnasaṃyuktāṃ saptadvīpavatīṃ mahīm .
śaśāsa dharmeṇa purā cakravartī mahābalaḥ . . 11
1.116.d:
स सर्वरत्नसंयुक्तां सप्तद्वीपवतीं महीम् ।
शशास धर्मेण पुरा चक्रवर्ती महाबलः ॥ 11
1.116.m: Endowed with all jewels, that emperor of great strength / formerly ruled according to dharma over the earth with its seven continents.

1.116.s:
nānyāyakṛnna cāśakto vadānyo balavattaraḥ .
tasyābhūtpuruṣā rājñaḥ samyagdharmānuśāsinaḥ . . 12
1.116.d:
नान्यायकृन्न चाशक्तो वदान्यो बलवत्तरः ।
तस्याभूत्पुरुषा राज्ञः सम्यग्धर्मानुशासिनः ॥ 12
1.116.m: He did no injustice, nor was he weak; he was generous and exceedingly strong. / That king had officers who properly enforced righteous conduct.

1.116.s:
catvāraḥ sacivāstasya rājñaḥ satrājitasya tu .
babhūvurapratihatāḥ sadā vāti balasya vai . . 13
1.116.d:
चत्वारः सचिवास्तस्य राज्ञः सत्राजितस्य तु ।
बभूवुरप्रतिहताः सदा वाति बलस्य वै ॥ 13
1.116.m: There were four ministers of that king Satrājit, / who were unhindered and ever directed his military force.

1.116.s:
tasya bhaktiratīvāsīnnisargādeva bhūpateḥ .
divākare jagadbhānau raktacandanamālini . . 14
1.116.d:
तस्य भक्तिरतीवासीन्निसर्गादेव भूपतेः ।
दिवाकरे जगद्भानौ रक्तचन्दनमालिनि ॥ 14
1.116.m: That lord of the earth had exceedingly great devotion, by his very nature, / to the Sun, the light of the universe, adorned with garlands of red sandalwood.

1.116.s:
tasyordhvamahimānaṃ ca vilokya pṛthivīpateḥ .
na kevalaṃ janasyāpi hyabhavattasya vismayaḥ . . 15
1.116.d:
तस्योर्ध्वमहिमानं च विलोक्य पृथिवीपतेः ।
न केवलं जनस्यापि ह्यभवत्तस्य विस्मयः ॥ 15
1.116.m: Beholding his supreme majesty, the lord of the earth / felt astonishment, and not he alone, but his people as well.

1.116.s:
sañcintayāmāsa nṛpaḥ samṛddhyā vismitastathā .
kathaṃ syāt sampadeṣā me punarapyanyajanmani . . 16
1.116.d:
सञ्चिन्तयामास नृपः समृद्ध्या विस्मितस्तथा ।
कथं स्यात् सम्पदेषा मे पुनरप्यन्यजन्मनि ॥ 16
1.116.m: Astonished by his prosperity, the king reflected: / 'How might this fortune be mine once again in another birth?'

1.116.s:
evaṃ sa bahuśo rājā tadā kṛṣṇa mahāyaśāḥ .
cintayannapi tanmūlaṃ nāsadanniścayānvitaḥ . . 17
1.116.d:
एवं स बहुशो राजा तदा कृष्ण महायशाः ।
चिन्तयन्नपि तन्मूलं नासदन्निश्चयान्वितः ॥ 17
1.116.m: In this way, O Kṛṣṇa, that highly renowned king then, / although thinking many times of its root cause, could not arrive at any certainty.

1.116.s:
yadā na niścayaṃ rājā sa yayau bhārgavīpriyaḥ .
tadā papraccha dharmajñānsa viprānsamupāgatān . . 18
1.116.d:
यदा न निश्चयं राजा स ययौ भार्गवीप्रियः ।
तदा पप्रच्छ धर्मज्ञान्स विप्रान्समुपागतान् ॥ 18
1.116.m: When the king, beloved of Bhārgavī, could reach no conclusion, / he then questioned the brahmins who had arrived, who were knowers of dharma.

1.116.s:
sarvāśca sasukhānvīra viviktāntaḥ purasthitaḥ .
praṇipatya mahābāhurgrahītuṃ śāsanakriyāḥ . . 19
1.116.d:
सर्वाश्च ससुखान्वीर विविक्तान्तः पुरस्थितः ।
प्रणिपत्य महाबाहुर्ग्रहीतुं शासनक्रियाः ॥ 19
1.116.m: Seated in the secluded inner quarters, the mighty-armed hero, / having bowed down to them all who were at ease, [spoke] to receive their instructions:

1.116.s:
viśvāsānugrahā buddhirbhavatāṃ mayi sattamāḥ .
tadahaṃ praṣṭumicchāmi kiñcittadvaktumarhatha . . 1.116.20
1.116.d:
विश्वासानुग्रहा बुद्धिर्भवतां मयि सत्तमाः ।
तदहं प्रष्टुमिच्छामि किञ्चित्तद्वक्तुमर्हथ ॥ 1.116.20
1.116.m: 'Your disposition toward me, O best of men, is one of trust and grace. / Therefore I wish to ask something; you ought to tell it to me.

1.116.s:
sadvidyākhilavijñānasamyagdhautāntarātmabhiḥ .
bhavadbhiryadyanugrāhyaḥ syāmahaṃ vedavittamāḥ . . 21
1.116.d:
सद्विद्याखिलविज्ञानसम्यग्धौतान्तरात्मभिः ।
भवद्भिर्यद्यनुग्राह्यः स्यामहं वेदवित्तमाः ॥ 21
1.116.m: If I am to be favoured by you whose inner selves are fully purified / by true knowledge and all discerning wisdom, O best among the knowers of the Veda,

1.116.s:
tadyathāvanmayā pṛṣṭā bhavanto matprasādinaḥ .
vaktumarhatha vidvāṃsaḥ sarvasyaivopakāriṇaḥ . . 22
1.116.d:
तद्यथावन्मया पृष्टा भवन्तो मत्प्रसादिनः ।
वक्तुमर्हथ विद्वांसः सर्वस्यैवोपकारिणः ॥ 22
1.116.m: then, when properly questioned by me, you who are gracious toward me, / who are learned and benefactors of all, ought to speak.'

1.116.s:
brahmovāca
yaste manasi sandehastaṃ pṛcchādya mahīpate .
vadiṣyāmo yathānyāyaṃ yatte1 manasi varttate . . 23
1.116.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यस्ते मनसि सन्देहस्तं पृच्छाद्य महीपते ।
वदिष्यामो यथान्यायं यत्ते1 मनसि वर्त्तते ॥ 23
1.116.m: [The brahmins] said: / 'Ask today, O lord of the earth, whatever doubt is in your mind; / we shall tell you according to propriety whatever dwells in your heart.

1.116.s:
vayaṃ hi nṛpaśārdūla bhavatā pāritoṣitāḥ .
samyakprajāṃ pālayitrā dadatā bhojanaṃ sadā . . 24
1.116.d:
वयं हि नृपशार्दूल भवता पारितोषिताः ।
सम्यक्प्रजां पालयित्रा ददता भोजनं सदा ॥ 24
1.116.m: For we, O tiger among kings, have been pleased by you, / who properly protect the subjects and constantly give food.

1.116.s:
santuṣṭo brāhmaṇo'śnīyācchiṃdyādvā dharmasaṃśayam .
hitaṃ copadiśedvartma ahitādvā nivartayet . . 25
1.116.d:
सन्तुष्टो ब्राह्मणोऽश्नीयाच्छिंद्याद्वा धर्मसंशयम् ।
हितं चोपदिशेद्वर्त्म अहिताद्वा निवर्तयेत् ॥ 25
1.116.m: A satisfied brahmin should eat, or he should resolve a doubt regarding dharma; / he should teach a beneficial path or turn [one] away from what is harmful.'

1.116.s:
vivakṣumatha bhūpālaṃ bhāryā tasyaiva dhīmataḥ .
praṇipātena cāhedaṃ vinayātpraṇayānvitam . . 26
1.116.d:
विवक्षुमथ भूपालं भार्या तस्यैव धीमतः ।
प्रणिपातेन चाहेदं विनयात्प्रणयान्वितम् ॥ 26
1.116.m: As the ruler of the earth was then about to speak, the wise king's wife, / with a bow and out of modesty filled with affection, said this:

1.116.s:
na strīṇāmavanīpāla vaktumīdṛgiheṣyate .
tathāpi bhūpate vakṣye sampadīdṛksudurlabhā . . 27
1.116.d:
न स्त्रीणामवनीपाल वक्तुमीदृगिहेष्यते ।
तथापि भूपते वक्ष्ये सम्पदीदृक्सुदुर्लभा ॥ 27
1.116.m: 'It is not considered fitting for women to speak like this here, O protector of the earth; / nevertheless, O king, I shall speak, for such fortune is extremely difficult to obtain.

1.116.s:
bhūyo'pi saṃśayānpraṣṭumalamīśo bhavānṛṣīn .
nanvahaṃ puraṣavyāghra sadāntaḥ puracāriṇī . . 28
1.116.d:
भूयोऽपि संशयान्प्रष्टुमलमीशो भवानृषीन् ।
नन्वहं पुरषव्याघ्र सदान्तः पुरचारिणी ॥ 28
1.116.m: You, my lord, are well able to ask the sages about your doubts again. / But I, O tiger among men, ever move only within the inner quarters.

1.116.s:
tatprasādaṃ yadi bhavānkaroti mama pārthiva .
tanmadīyamṛṣīnpraṣṭuṃ sandehaṃ pārthivārhasi . . 29
1.116.d:
तत्प्रसादं यदि भवान्करोति मम पार्थिव ।
तन्मदीयमृषीन्प्रष्टुं सन्देहं पार्थिवार्हसि ॥ 29
1.116.m: Therefore, if you would show me favour, O king, / you ought to ask the sages this doubt of mine, O ruler of the earth.'

1.116.s:
satrājita uvāca
brūhi subhrūrmataṃ yatte praṣṭavyā yanmayā dvijāḥ .
bhūyo'hamātmasandehaṃ prakṣyāmyetaddvijottamān . . 1.116.30
1.116.d:
सत्राजित उवाच
ब्रूहि सुभ्रूर्मतं यत्ते प्रष्टव्या यन्मया द्विजाः ।
भूयोऽहमात्मसन्देहं प्रक्ष्याम्येतद्द्विजोत्तमान् ॥ 1.116.30
1.116.m: Satrājit said: / 'Speak, O fair-browed one, what you think the twice-born should be asked by me; / afterwards I shall ask these best of the twice-born my own doubt.'

1.116.s:
vimalavatyuvāca
śrūyante pṛthivīpāla nṛpā ye tu cirantanāḥ .
yeṣāṃ ca sampadbhūpāla yathā te'dya kilābhavat . . 31
1.116.d:
विमलवत्युवाच
श्रूयन्ते पृथिवीपाल नृपा ये तु चिरन्तनाः ।
येषां च सम्पद्भूपाल यथा तेऽद्य किलाभवत् ॥ 31
1.116.m: Vimalavatī said: / 'O protector of the earth, we hear of kings of old / who possessed such fortune, O king, as is yours today.

1.116.s:
tadīdṛksampado dhāma tavāśeṣaṃ kṣitīśvara .
yena karmavipākena tadvadantu maharṣayaḥ . . 32
1.116.d:
तदीदृक्सम्पदो धाम तवाशेषं क्षितीश्वर ।
येन कर्मविपाकेन तद्वदन्तु महर्षयः ॥ 32
1.116.m: By the fruition of what deed did all of this abode of such fortune / become yours, O lord of the earth? Let the great sages tell that.

1.116.s:
ahaṃ ca bhavato bhāryā sarvasīmantinīvarā .
atīva karmaṇā yena tadvijñāne kutūhalam . . 33
1.116.d:
अहं च भवतो भार्या सर्वसीमन्तिनीवरा ।
अतीव कर्मणा येन तद्विज्ञाने कुतूहलम् ॥ 33
1.116.m: And by what extraordinary deed did I become your wife, / the best of all women with parted hair? I have a curiosity to know that.

1.116.s:
tathā sampatsamṛddhatvamanyeṣvapi hi vidyate .
nirastātiśayatvena nūnaṃ nālpena karmaṇā . . 34
1.116.d:
तथा सम्पत्समृद्धत्वमन्येष्वपि हि विद्यते ।
निरस्तातिशयत्वेन नूनं नाल्पेन कर्मणा ॥ 34
1.116.m: Likewise, abundance of fortune is found in others too, / but this unsurpassed nature [of yours] is surely not due to a trivial deed.

1.116.s:
tadanyajanmacaritaṃ naranātha nijaṃ bhavān .
munīnpṛccha tvayā cāhaṃ yanmayā ca purā kṛtam . . 35
1.116.d:
तदन्यजन्मचरितं नरनाथ निजं भवान् ।
मुनीन्पृच्छ त्वया चाहं यन्मया च पुरा कृतम् ॥ 35
1.116.m: Therefore, O lord of men, ask the sages about your own deeds in another birth, / and what was done previously by you and by me.'

1.116.s:
brahmovāca
sa tathoktastayā rājā patnyā vismitamānasaḥ .
munīnāṃ purato māyāṃ praśaṃsanvākyamabravīt . . 36
1.116.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
स तथोक्तस्तया राजा पत्न्या विस्मितमानसः ।
मुनीनां पुरतो मायां प्रशंसन्वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ 36
1.116.m: Brahmā said: / Having been addressed in this way by his wife, the king, with wonder in his heart, / praising her cleverness before the sages, spoke these words:

1.116.s:
sādhu devi mataṃ yanme tvayā yadidamīritam .
satyaṃ munivacaḥ puṃsāṃ syāddha vai gṛhiṇī tathā . . 37
1.116.d:
साधु देवि मतं यन्मे त्वया यदिदमीरितम् ।
सत्यं मुनिवचः पुंसां स्याद्ध वै गृहिणी तथा ॥ 37
1.116.m: 'Noble is your thought, O queen, which has been spoken by you! / True is the sages' word that a housewife is indeed [a partner in dharma] for men.

1.116.s:
so'hametanmahābhāge pṛcchāmyetānmahāmunīn .
teṣāmaviditaṃ kiñcittriṣu lokeṣu na vidyate . . 38
1.116.d:
सोऽहमेतन्महाभागे पृच्छाम्येतान्महामुनीन् ।
तेषामविदितं किञ्चित्त्रिषु लोकेषु न विद्यते ॥ 38
1.116.m: Therefore, O highly fortunate one, I shall ask these great sages; / there is nothing in the three worlds that is unknown to them.'

1.116.s:
evamuktvā priyāṃ rājā praṇipatya ca tānṛṣīn .
yathāvadetadakhilaṃ papraccha dharaṇīdharaḥ . . 39
1.116.d:
एवमुक्त्वा प्रियां राजा प्रणिपत्य च तानृषीन् ।
यथावदेतदखिलं पप्रच्छ धरणीधरः ॥ 39
1.116.m: Having spoken thus to his beloved, and having bowed down to those sages, / the sustainer of the earth asked all this in accordance with proper rule.

1.116.s:
rājovāca
bhagavanto mamāśeṣaṃ prasādāvṛtacetasaḥ .
kathayantu yathāvṛttaṃ yanmayā sukṛtaṃ kṛtam . .1.116.4 0
ko'hamāsaṃ purā viprāḥ kiṃsvitkarma mayā kṛtam .
kiṃ vānayā tu cārvaṃgyā mama patnyā kṛtaṃ dvijāḥ . .4 1
yenāvayoriyaṃ lakṣmīrmartyaloke sudurlabhā .
catvāraścāpratihatā amātyā mama gacchataḥ . .4 2
aśeṣā bhūbhṛto vaśyā dhanasyānto na vidyate .
balaṃ caivāpratihataṃ śarīrārogyameva ca . .4 3
pratibhāti ca me kāntyā bhāryāyāmakhilaṃ jagat .
mamāpi vapuṣastejo na kaścitsahate dvijāḥ .44
1.116.d:
राजोवाच
भगवन्तो ममाशेषं प्रसादावृतचेतसः ।
कथयन्तु यथावृत्तं यन्मया सुकृतं कृतम् ॥1.116.4 0
कोऽहमासं पुरा विप्राः किंस्वित्कर्म मया कृतम् ।
किं वानया तु चार्वंग्या मम पत्न्या कृतं द्विजाः ॥4 1
येनावयोरियं लक्ष्मीर्मर्त्यलोके सुदुर्लभा ।
चत्वारश्चाप्रतिहता अमात्या मम गच्छतः ॥4 2
अशेषा भूभृतो वश्या धनस्यान्तो न विद्यते ।
बलं चैवाप्रतिहतं शरीरारोग्यमेव च ॥4 3
प्रतिभाति च मे कान्त्या भार्यायामखिलं जगत् ।
ममापि वपुषस्तेजो न कश्चित्सहते द्विजाः .44
1.116.m:
The king said:
May your reverences, with minds enveloped in grace,
relate to me fully as it happened the virtuous deed that was done by me.
Who was I in the past, O brāhmaṇas? What action indeed was performed by me,
or what was done by this slender-limbed wife of mine, O twice-born ones,
by which this fortune, so very difficult to attain in the mortal world, belongs to the two of us,
and four ministers, unopposed, attend me as I proceed,
all kings are submissive, there is no end to wealth,
and my strength is irresistible, as is the health of my body?
And the entire world seems radiant to me in my wife by her beauty,
and no one can endure the lustre of my body as well, O twice-born ones.

1.116.s:
so'hamicchāmi tajjñātuṃ tathaiveyamaninditā .
nijānuṣṭhānamakhilaṃ yasyāśeṣamidaṃ phalam . .45
1.116.d:
सोऽहमिच्छामि तज्ज्ञातुं तथैवेयमनिन्दिता ।
निजानुष्ठानमखिलं यस्याशेषमिदं फलम् ॥45
1.116.m:
Therefore I wish to know that, and likewise this blameless woman [wishes to know],
the entirety of her own practice, of which all this is the fruit.

1.116.s:
brahmovāca
iti pṛṣṭā narendreṇa samastāste tapodhanāḥ .
parāvasumathocuste kathyatāmasya bhūbhṛtaḥ . . 46
1.116.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इति पृष्टा नरेन्द्रेण समस्तास्ते तपोधनाः ।
परावसुमथोचुस्ते कथ्यतामस्य भूभृतः ॥ 46
1.116.m:
Brahmā said:
Having been thus questioned by the king, all those ascetics
then said to Parāvasu: “Let it be told to this king.”

1.116.s:
coditaḥ so'pi dharmajñairmahāśūrā mahāmatiḥ .
yogamāsthāya suciraṃ yathāvadyatamānasaḥ . . 47
1.116.d:
चोदितः सोऽपि धर्मज्ञैर्महाशूरा महामतिः ।
योगमास्थाय सुचिरं यथावद्यतमानसः ॥ 47
1.116.m:
Urged by those who knew dharma, he too, a great hero and of great intellect,
having entered into yoga for a very long time, with his mind suitably restrained,

1.116.s:
jñātavānnṛpatestasya pūrvadehaviceṣṭitam .
sa tamāha munirbhūpaṃ vijñānecchaṃ mahāmatim . . 48
1.116.d:
ज्ञातवान्नृपतेस्तस्य पूर्वदेहविचेष्टितम् ।
स तमाह मुनिर्भूपं विज्ञानेच्छं महामतिम् ॥ 48
1.116.m:
perceived the conduct of that king in his previous body.
That sage spoke to the king, of great intellect, who desired knowledge,

1.116.s:
satrājitaṃ mahātmānaṃ jitaśatruṃ manasvinam .
sapatnīkaṃ mahābuddhiṃ brāhmaṇānsatyavādinaḥ . . 49
1.116.d:
सत्राजितं महात्मानं जितशत्रुं मनस्विनम् ।
सपत्नीकं महाबुद्धिं ब्राह्मणान्सत्यवादिनः ॥ 49
1.116.m:
to the high-souled Satrājit, who had conquered his enemies, who was wise,
accompanied by his wife, exceedingly intelligent, [and surrounded by] truthful brāhmaṇas.

1.116.s:
parāvasuruvāca
śṛṇu bhūpāla sakalaṃ yasyedaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam .
tava rājyādikaṃ subhrūryeyaṃ cāsīnmahīpate . . 1.116.50
1.116.d:
परावसुरुवाच
शृणु भूपाल सकलं यस्येदं कर्मणः फलम् ।
तव राज्यादिकं सुभ्रूर्येयं चासीन्महीपते ॥ 1.116.50
1.116.m:
Parāvasu said:
Listen, O protector of the earth, to everything of which action this is the fruit—
your sovereignty and the rest, and this fair-browed woman who was [yours], O king.

1.116.s:
tvamāsīḥ śūdrajātīyaḥ parahiṃsāparāyaṇaḥ .
kuṣṭhārto daṇḍapāruṣye niḥsnehaḥ sarvajantuṣu . . 51
1.116.d:
त्वमासीः शूद्रजातीयः परहिंसापरायणः ।
कुष्ठार्तो दण्डपारुष्ये निःस्नेहः सर्वजन्तुषु ॥ 51
1.116.m:
You were of the Śūdra caste, devoted to harming others,
afflicted with leprosy, given to harsh punishment, devoid of affection for all creatures.

1.116.s:
dvayaṃ ca bhavato bhāryā pūrvamapyāyatekṣaṇā .
nityaṃ babhūva tvaccittā bhavacchuśrūṣaṇe ratā . . 52
1.116.d:
द्वयं च भवतो भार्या पूर्वमप्यायतेक्षणा ।
नित्यं बभूव त्वच्चित्ता भवच्छुश्रूषणे रता ॥ 52
1.116.m:
And the wife of your honour, even previously, was this long-eyed one;
constantly she was devoted to you in mind, delighting in serving your honour,

1.116.s:
pativratā mahābhāgā bhartsyamānāpi niṣṭhuram .
tvadvākyeṣu ca sarveṣu vīra karmasu codyatā . 53
1.116.d:
पतिव्रता महाभागा भर्त्स्यमानापि निष्ठुरम् ।
त्वद्वाक्येषु च सर्वेषु वीर कर्मसु चोद्यता । 53
1.116.m:
a devoted wife of great fortune, even though harshly berated,
and ever zealous, O hero, in all your words and deeds.

1.116.s:
naiśvaryādasahāyasya tyajyamānasya bandhubhiḥ .
kṣayaṃ jagāma yortho'bhūtsañcitaḥ prapitāmahaiḥ . . 54
1.116.d:
नैश्वर्यादसहायस्य त्यज्यमानस्य बन्धुभिः ।
क्षयं जगाम योर्थोऽभूत्सञ्चितः प्रपितामहैः ॥ 54
1.116.m:
Because of lack of wealth for you who were without support and abandoned by your relatives,
whatever wealth had been accumulated by your great-grandfathers went to ruin.

1.116.s:
tasminkṣīṇe kṛṣiparastvamāsīḥ pṛthivīpate .
sāpi karmavipākena kṛṣirviphalatāṃ gatā . . 55
1.116.d:
तस्मिन्क्षीणे कृषिपरस्त्वमासीः पृथिवीपते ।
सापि कर्मविपाकेन कृषिर्विफलतां गता ॥ 55
1.116.m:
When that was depleted, you became devoted to agriculture, O lord of the earth.
That agriculture too came to fruitlessness through the ripening of [past] deeds.

1.116.s:
tato niḥsvaṃ parikṣīṇaṃ pareṣāṃ bhṛtyatāṃ gatam .
tatyāja sādhvī neyaṃ tvāṃ tyajyamānāpi pārthiva . . 56
1.116.d:
ततो निःस्वं परिक्षीणं परेषां भृत्यतां गतम् ।
तत्याज साध्वी नेयं त्वां त्यज्यमानापि पार्थिव ॥ 56
1.116.m:
Then, when you were destitute, utterly ruined, and reduced to servitude to others,
this virtuous woman did not abandon you, O king, even though she was being abandoned [by all].

1.116.s:
anayā tu samaṃ sādhvyā bhānorāvasathe tvayā .
kṛtaṃ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ vṛttyā bhaktyā sammārjanādikam . . 57
1.116.d:
अनया तु समं साध्व्या भानोरावसथे त्वया ।
कृतं शुश्रूषणं वृत्त्या भक्त्या सम्मार्जनादिकम् ॥ 57
1.116.m:
Together with this virtuous woman, in the abode of the sun,
service was performed by you by way of livelihood [and] through devotion, such as sweeping and the like.

1.116.s:
niḥsnehaḥ sarvakāmebhyastanmayastvaṃ tadarpaṇaḥ .
ahanyahani visrambhāttasminnāvasathe raveḥ . . 58
1.116.d:
निःस्नेहः सर्वकामेभ्यस्तन्मयस्त्वं तदर्पणः ।
अहन्यहनि विस्रम्भात्तस्मिन्नावसथे रवेः ॥ 58
1.116.m:
Free from attachment to all desires, absorbed in Him, dedicated to Him,
day after day, with trust in that abode of the sun,

1.116.s:
kānyakubjapure vīra mahāśuśrūṣitaṃ tvayā .
divākarālaye nityaṃ kṛtaṃ tanmārjanaṃ tvayā . . 59
1.116.d:
कान्यकुब्जपुरे वीर महाशुश्रूषितं त्वया ।
दिवाकरालये नित्यं कृतं तन्मार्जनं त्वया ॥ 59
1.116.m:
in the city of Kānyakubja, O hero, great service was rendered by you;
in the temple of the sun, sweeping was constantly done by you.

1.116.s:
tathaivābhyukṣaṇaṃ bhūpa nityaṃ caivānulepanam .
patnyānayā nṛpa tathā yuṣmaccittānuvṛttayā . . 1.116.60
1.116.d:
तथैवाभ्युक्षणं भूप नित्यं चैवानुलेपनम् ।
पत्न्यानया नृप तथा युष्मच्चित्तानुवृत्तया ॥ 1.116.60
1.116.m:
Likewise sprinkling, O king, and constant smearing [with cow dung],
was thus done by this wife, O king, who followed your mind.

1.116.s:
kāritaṃ śravaṇaṃ puṇyamitihāsapurāṇayoḥ .
dattvāṅgulīyakaṃ rājanpitṛdattaṃ tu vācake . . 61
1.116.d:
कारितं श्रवणं पुण्यमितिहासपुराणयोः ।
दत्त्वाङ्गुलीयकं राजन्पितृदत्तं तु वाचके ॥ 61
1.116.m:
The meritorious hearing of the itihāsas and purāṇas was arranged,
after giving to the reciter a ring given by your father, O king.

1.116.s:
ahanyahani yatkarma yuvayornṛpakurvatoḥ .
tatraiva tanmayatvena pāpahānirajāyata . . 62
1.116.d:
अहन्यहनि यत्कर्म युवयोर्नृपकुर्वतोः ।
तत्रैव तन्मयत्वेन पापहानिरजायत ॥ 62
1.116.m:
Day after day, as the two of you performed that work, O king,
there itself, through being absorbed in that, the destruction of your sin took place.

1.116.s:
bhānoḥ kāryaṃ mayā kāryaṃ paraṃ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ tathā .
nāprabhātaṃ prabhātaṃ vā cinteyamabhavanniśi . . 63
1.116.d:
भानोः कार्यं मया कार्यं परं शुश्रूषणं तथा ।
नाप्रभातं प्रभातं वा चिन्तेयमभवन्निशि ॥ 63
1.116.m:
“The business of the sun must be done by me, and supreme service likewise”;
neither before dawn nor after dawn did this reflection leave you at night.

1.116.s:
evamāyatanaṃ ramyamityevaṃ ca sukhāvaham .
sūryavaccaivametatsyādityāsītte manastadā . . 64
1.116.d:
एवमायतनं रम्यमित्येवं च सुखावहम् ।
सूर्यवच्चैवमेतत्स्यादित्यासीत्ते मनस्तदा ॥ 64
1.116.m:
“May the temple thus be charming, and thus bring happiness,
and may it be like the sun!”—such was your mind at that time.

1.116.s:
yogināṃ sukhadaṃ karma tathaiva sukhamityapi .
bhavaccittamabhūttatra yogakarmaṇyaharniśam . . 65
1.116.d:
योगिनां सुखदं कर्म तथैव सुखमित्यपि ।
भवच्चित्तमभूत्तत्र योगकर्मण्यहर्निशम् ॥ 65
1.116.m:
“Action that gives joy to yogins is likewise bliss”—
such was your mind there, day and night in the practice of yoga.

1.116.s:
evaṃ tanmanasastatra kṛtodyogasya pārthiva .
bhūtānumāninaḥ samyagyathoktādhikakāriṇaḥ . . 66
1.116.d:
एवं तन्मनसस्तत्र कृतोद्योगस्य पार्थिव ।
भूतानुमानिनः सम्यग्यथोक्ताधिककारिणः ॥ 66
1.116.m:
Thus, with your mind fixed upon it, exerting yourself there, O king,
respectful toward living beings, performing properly more than what was prescribed,

1.116.s:
smarato gopatiṃ nityaṃ cittenāpi dṛḍhātmanaḥ .
niḥśeṣamupaśāṃtaṃ te pāpaṃ sūryaniṣevaṇāt . . 67
1.116.d:
स्मरतो गोपतिं नित्यं चित्तेनापि दृढात्मनः ।
निःशेषमुपशांतं ते पापं सूर्यनिषेवणात् ॥ 67
1.116.m:
constantly remembering the lord of rays with a mind that was resolute in spirit,
your sin was completely appeased through attendance upon the sun.

1.116.s:
tato'dhikaṃ purastasmādagārasyānulepanam .
saṃmārjanaṃ ca bahuśaḥ sapatnīkena yatkṛtam . . 68
1.116.d:
ततोऽधिकं पुरस्तस्मादगारस्यानुलेपनम् ।
संमार्जनं च बहुशः सपत्नीकेन यत्कृतम् ॥ 68
1.116.m:
Even more than before, the smearing of that house
and repeated sweeping was done [by you] together with your wife.

1.116.s:
kevalaṃ dharmamāśritya tyaktvā vṛttimaśeṣataḥ .
anayā śravaṇaṃ puṇyaṃ kāritaṃ vācakātsadā . 69
1.116.d:
केवलं धर्ममाश्रित्य त्यक्त्वा वृत्तिमशेषतः ।
अनया श्रवणं पुण्यं कारितं वाचकात्सदा । 69
1.116.m:
Relying purely on dharma, having abandoned all other livelihood,
the meritorious hearing from the reciter was constantly arranged by her.

1.116.s:
nānādhātuvikāraistu gomayena mṛdā tathā .
upalepanaṃ kṛtaṃ bhaktyā tvayā pūrvaṃ surālaye . . 1.116.70
1.116.d:
नानाधातुविकारैस्तु गोमयेन मृदा तथा ।
उपलेपनं कृतं भक्त्या त्वया पूर्वं सुरालये ॥ 1.116.70
1.116.m:
With preparations of various minerals, and with cow dung and clay,
smearing was previously done with devotion by you in the temple of the deity.

1.116.s:
athājagāma vai tatra kuvalāśvo mahīpatiḥ .
mahāsainyaparīvāraḥ prabhūtagajavāhanaḥ . . 71
1.116.d:
अथाजगाम वै तत्र कुवलाश्वो महीपतिः ।
महासैन्यपरीवारः प्रभूतगजवाहनः ॥ 71
1.116.m:
Then indeed King Kuvalāśva came there,
accompanied by a vast army and having abundant elephant-mounts.

1.116.s:
sarvasampadupetaṃ taṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam .
vṛtaṃ bhāryāsahasreṇa dṛṣṭvā saṃkrandanodbalam . .
spṛhā kṛtā tvayā tatra cārumaulini pārthive . . 72
1.116.d:
सर्वसम्पदुपेतं तं सर्वाभरणभूषितम् ।
वृतं भार्यासहस्रेण दृष्ट्वा संक्रन्दनोद्बलम् ॥
स्पृहा कृता त्वया तत्र चारुमौलिनि पार्थिवे ॥ 72
1.116.m:
Seeing him endowed with all prosperity, adorned with all ornaments,
surrounded by a thousand wives, possessed of the might of Indra,
a longing was formed by you for that king with his beautiful diadem.

1.116.s:
sarvakāmapradaṃ karma kriyate bhāskārāśritam .
tenaitadakhilaṃ rājyamaśeṣaṃ cāptavānmahīm . . 73
1.116.d:
सर्वकामप्रदं कर्म क्रियते भास्काराश्रितम् ।
तेनैतदखिलं राज्यमशेषं चाप्तवान्महीम् ॥ 73
1.116.m:
Action that bestows all desires, directed to the sun, is performed;
by that you obtained this entire kingdom and the whole earth.

1.116.s:
tejaścaivādhikaṃ yatte tathaiva śṛṇu pārthiva .
yogaprabhāvato labdhaṃ kathayāmyakhilaṃ tava . . 74
1.116.d:
तेजश्चैवाधिकं यत्ते तथैव शृणु पार्थिव ।
योगप्रभावतो लब्धं कथयाम्यखिलं तव ॥ 74
1.116.m:
And hear likewise, O king, about the extraordinary lustre that is yours,
obtained by the power of yoga; I shall tell you all of it.

1.116.s:
tatraivāvasathe dīpaḥ praśāntaḥ snehasaṃkṣayāt .
nijabhojanatailena punaḥ prajvalitastvayā . . 75
1.116.d:
तत्रैवावसथे दीपः प्रशान्तः स्नेहसंक्षयात् ।
निजभोजनतैलेन पुनः प्रज्वलितस्त्वया ॥ 75
1.116.m:
In that very abode, a lamp had gone out from the exhaustion of oil;
it was lit again by you with the oil of your own food.

1.116.s:
anyā cottarīyeṇa vīra vartyopabṛṃhitaḥ .
tava patnyā svayaṃ jvālya kāntirasyāstato'dhikā . . 76
1.116.d:
अन्या चोत्तरीयेण वीर वर्त्योपबृंहितः ।
तव पत्न्या स्वयं ज्वाल्य कान्तिरस्यास्ततोऽधिका ॥ 76
1.116.m:
And augmented with another wick from her upper garment, O hero,
it was lit by your wife herself; hence her beauty is superior to that.

1.116.s:
tavāpyakhilabhūpālamanaḥ kṣobhakaraṃ punaḥ .
tejo narendra etasmātkimutārādhya bhāskaram . . 77
1.116.d:
तवाप्यखिलभूपालमनः क्षोभकरं पुनः ।
तेजो नरेन्द्र एतस्मात्किमुताराध्य भास्करम् ॥ 77
1.116.m:
Your lustre also, O lord of men, which agitates the minds of all kings,
is from this—how much more so from having worshiped the sun!

1.116.s:
evaṃ narendraḥ śūdratvādbhānukarmaparāyaṇaḥ .
tanmayatvena samprāpto mahimānamanuttamam . . 78
1.116.d:
एवं नरेन्द्रः शूद्रत्वाद्भानुकर्मपरायणः ।
तन्मयत्वेन सम्प्राप्तो महिमानमनुत्तमम् ॥ 78
1.116.m:
Thus, from being a Śūdra, the king became devoted to the work of the sun;
through being absorbed in Him, he attained unsurpassed greatness.

1.116.s:
kiṃ punaryo naro bhaktyā nityaṃ śuśrūṣaṇāvṛtaḥ .
karoti satataṃ pūjāṃ niṣkāmo nānyamānasaḥ . . 79
1.116.d:
किं पुनर्यो नरो भक्त्या नित्यं शुश्रूषणावृतः ।
करोति सततं पूजां निष्कामो नान्यमानसः ॥ 79
1.116.m:
How much more then does that man, who with devotion, constantly filled with service,
perpetually performs worship, desireless and with no other thought in mind!

1.116.s:
sarvāmṛddhimimāṃ labdhvā sarvalokamaheśvaraḥ .
pūjayitvārkamīśeśaṃ tamārādhya na sīdati . . 1.116.80
1.116.d:
सर्वामृद्धिमिमां लब्ध्वा सर्वलोकमहेश्वरः ।
पूजयित्वार्कमीशेशं तमाराध्य न सीदति ॥ 1.116.80
1.116.m:
Having obtained all this prosperity, a great lord over all people,
having worshiped the sun, the lord of lords, and having venerated Him, he does not suffer.

1.116.s:
puṣpai dhūpaistathā vānyairdīpairvastrānulepanaiḥ .
ārādhayārkaṃ tadveśma sadā sammārjanādinā . . 81
1.116.d:
पुष्पै धूपैस्तथा वान्यैर्दीपैर्वस्त्रानुलेपनैः ।
आराधयार्कं तद्वेश्म सदा सम्मार्जनादिना ॥ 81
1.116.m:
With flowers, with incenses, or with other lamps, garments, and unguents,
worship the sun, and His temple always with sweeping and the like.

1.116.s:
yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ kiñcidyadyanyattu durlabham .
taddatvā ca jagaddhātre bhāskarāya na sīdati . . 82
1.116.d:
यद्यदिष्टतमं किञ्चिद्यद्यन्यत्तु दुर्लभम् ।
तद्दत्वा च जगद्धात्रे भास्कराय न सीदति ॥ 82
1.116.m:
Whatever is most beloved, or whatever else is difficult to obtain,
by giving that to the sun, the sustainer of the world, one does not suffer.

1.116.s:
sugandhāgurukarpūracandanāgurukuṃkumaiḥ .
vāsobhirvividhairdhūpaiḥ puṣpaiḥ srakcāmaradhvajaiḥ . . 83
1.116.d:
सुगन्धागुरुकर्पूरचन्दनागुरुकुंकुमैः ।
वासोभिर्विविधैर्धूपैः पुष्पैः स्रक्चामरध्वजैः ॥ 83
1.116.m:
With fragrant agallochum, camphor, sandalwood, aloe, and saffron,
with various garments and incenses, with flowers, garlands, chowries, and banners,

1.116.s:
anyopahārairvividhaiḥ kṛtakṣīrābhiṣecanaiḥ .
gītavāditranṛtyādyaistoṣayasvārkamādarāt . . 84
1.116.d:
अन्योपहारैर्विविधैः कृतक्षीराभिषेचनैः ।
गीतवादित्रनृत्याद्यैस्तोषयस्वार्कमादरात् ॥ 84
1.116.m:
with other various offerings, with performed milk-ablutions,
and with songs, musical instruments, and dances, gratify the sun with reverence.

1.116.s:
puṇyarātriṣu mārtaṇḍaṃ nṛtyagītairathojjvalam .
bhūpa jāgaraṇairbhaktyā homaḥ kāryaḥ sadā śuciḥ . . 85
1.116.d:
पुण्यरात्रिषु मार्तण्डं नृत्यगीतैरथोज्ज्वलम् ।
भूप जागरणैर्भक्त्या होमः कार्यः सदा शुचिः ॥ 85
1.116.m: On holy nights, O king, [worship] Mārtaṇḍa, made radiant with dancing and singing / and with vigils, by devotion; a pure oblation must always be performed,

1.116.s:
itihāsapurāṇānāṃ śravaṇena .viśeṣataḥ .
tathā vedasvanaiḥ puṇyairṛksāmayajubhirnṛpa . . 86
1.116.d:
इतिहासपुराणानां श्रवणेन ।विशेषतः ।
तथा वेदस्वनैः पुण्यैरृक्सामयजुभिर्नृप ॥ 86
1.116.m: especially through the hearing of histories and Purāṇas, / and likewise, O king, with the holy Vedic chants of the Ṛg, Sāman, and Yajus.

1.116.s:
evaṃ santoṣyate bhaktyā bhagavānbhavabhaṅgakṛt .
bhūyo vaivasvato bhūtvā bhavahṛdbhāskaro naraiḥ .. 87
1.116.d:
एवं सन्तोष्यते भक्त्या भगवान्भवभङ्गकृत् ।
भूयो वैवस्वतो भूत्वा भवहृद्भास्करो नरैः ॥ 87
1.116.m: Thus the blessed destroyer of worldly existence is pleased through devotion / by human beings, and the sun, dispelling worldly existence, becomes their protector.

1.116.s:
toṣito bhagavānbhānurdadātyabhimataṃ phalam .
daivakarmasamarthānāṃ prāṇināṃ smṛtisambhavaiḥ . . 88
1.116.d:
तोषितो भगवान्भानुर्ददात्यभिमतं फलम् ।
दैवकर्मसमर्थानां प्राणिनां स्मृतिसम्भवैः ॥ 88
1.116.m: When pleased, the blessed Sun grants their desired fruit / through [deeds] born of memory, to living beings capable of divine rites.

1.116.s:
toṣito bhagavānkāmānprayacchati divākaraḥ .
naiṣa vṛttairna ratnaughaiḥ puṣpairdhūpānulepanaiḥ . .
sadbhāvenaiva mārtaṇḍastoṣamāyāti saṃsmṛtaḥ . . 89
1.116.d:
तोषितो भगवान्कामान्प्रयच्छति दिवाकरः ।
नैष वृत्तैर्न रत्नौघैः पुष्पैर्धूपानुलेपनैः ॥
सद्भावेनैव मार्तण्डस्तोषमायाति संस्मृतः ॥ 89
1.116.m: When pleased, the blessed maker of day bestows their desires. / Not by conduct, nor by heaps of jewels, nor by flowers, incense, or unguents, / but solely through sincere faith does Mārtaṇḍa attain delight when remembered.

1.116.s:
tvayaikāgramanaskena gṛhasammārjanādikam .
kṛtvālpamīdṛśaṃ prāptaṃ rājyamanyena durlabham . . 1.116.90
1.116.d:
त्वयैकाग्रमनस्केन गृहसम्मार्जनादिकम् ।
कृत्वाल्पमीदृशं प्राप्तं राज्यमन्येन दुर्लभम् ॥ 1.116.90
1.116.m: By sweeping the house and doing other small services with a focused mind, / such a kingdom, unattainable by another, was attained by you.

1.116.s:
anayā śravaṇaṃ puṇyaṃ kārayitvā gṛhe raveḥ .
īdṛkprāptā sampadiyaṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā tu vācake . . 91
1.116.d:
अनया श्रवणं पुण्यं कारयित्वा गृहे रवेः ।
ईदृक्प्राप्ता सम्पदियं पूजां कृत्वा तु वाचके ॥ 91
1.116.m: By her, having arranged holy recitation in the house of the Sun / and having worshipped the reciter, this sort of fortune was obtained.

1.116.s:
prāptopakaraṇairyastamekāgramatiraṇḍajam .
santoṣayati nendro'pi bhavatā vai samaḥ kvacit . . 92
1.116.d:
प्राप्तोपकरणैर्यस्तमेकाग्रमतिरण्डजम् ।
सन्तोषयति नेन्द्रोऽपि भवता वै समः क्वचित् ॥ 92
1.116.m: Whoever, with a single-pointed mind, satisfies that egg-born god with the requisites at hand— / truly not even Indra is anywhere equal to you.

1.116.s:
tasmāttvamanayā devyā sahātyantavinītayā .
bhāskarārādhane yatnaṃ kuru dharmabhṛtāṃ vara . . 93
1.116.d:
तस्मात्त्वमनया देव्या सहात्यन्तविनीतया ।
भास्कराराधने यत्नं कुरु धर्मभृतां वर ॥ 93
1.116.m: Therefore, together with this exceedingly modest queen, / make an effort in the worship of the Sun, O best of the upholders of righteousness!

1.116.s:
brahmovāca
etanmunervaco vīra niśamya sa narādhipaḥ .
bhāryāsahāyaḥ sa tadā saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ . . 94
1.116.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतन्मुनेर्वचो वीर निशम्य स नराधिपः ।
भार्यासहायः स तदा संप्रहृष्टतनूरुहः ॥ 94
1.116.m:
Brahmā said:
Having heard these words of the sage, O hero, that ruler of men, / together with his wife, had the hair of his body stand on end with joy.

1.116.s:
kṛtakāryamivātmānaṃ manyamānastadābhavat .
uvāca praṇato bhūtvā rājā satrājito'cyuta . . 95
1.116.d:
कृतकार्यमिवात्मानं मन्यमानस्तदाभवत् ।
उवाच प्रणतो भूत्वा राजा सत्राजितोऽच्युत ॥ 95
1.116.m: Thinking of himself as one who had accomplished his goal, / King Satrājita bowed down and spoke, O infallible one.

1.116.s:
satrājita uvāca
yathāmaratvaṃ samprāpya yathā vāyurbalaṃ param .
paraṃ nirvāṇamāpnoti tathāhaṃ vacasā tava . . 96
1.116.d:
सत्राजित उवाच
यथामरत्वं सम्प्राप्य यथा वायुर्बलं परम् ।
परं निर्वाणमाप्नोति तथाहं वचसा तव ॥ 96
1.116.m:
Satrājita said:
Just as one attains immortality, or just as the wind attains supreme strength / and reaches the highest liberation, so have I by your words.

1.116.s:
kṛtakṛtyaḥ sukhāsīno nirvṛtiṃ paramāṃ gataḥ .
ajñānatamasācchanne yatpradīpastvayā dhṛtaḥ . . 97
1.116.d:
कृतकृत्यः सुखासीनो निर्वृतिं परमां गतः ।
अज्ञानतमसाच्छन्ने यत्प्रदीपस्त्वया धृतः ॥ 97
1.116.m: I am fulfilled, seated happily, having reached supreme peace, / because you held up a lamp where there was darkness of ignorance.

1.116.s:
ahameṣā ca tanvaṅgī vibhūtibhraṃśabhīrukaḥ .
dravyamāpāditaṃ brahmannihādya vacasā tava . . 98
1.116.d:
अहमेषा च तन्वङ्गी विभूतिभ्रंशभीरुकः ।
द्रव्यमापादितं ब्रह्मन्निहाद्य वचसा तव ॥ 98
1.116.m: I, fearful of losing prosperity, and this slender-bodied [queen]— / wealth has been provided to us here today, O holy one, by your words.

1.116.s:
sampadaḥ kathitaṃ bījamāvayorbhavatā mune .
tvadvaktrādudyatā vāco vijñātā hi dvijottama . . 99
1.116.d:
सम्पदः कथितं बीजमावयोर्भवता मुने ।
त्वद्वक्त्रादुद्यता वाचो विज्ञाता हि द्विजोत्तम ॥ 99
1.116.m: The root of fortune for both of us has been spoken by you, O sage; / the words spoken from your mouth have indeed been understood, O best of the twice-born.

1.116.s:
na ratnairna ca vittaughairna ca puṣpānulepanaiḥ .
ārādhyaśca jagannātho bhāvaśūnyairdivākaraḥ . . 1.116.100
1.116.d:
न रत्नैर्न च वित्तौघैर्न च पुष्पानुलेपनैः ।
आराध्यश्च जगन्नाथो भावशून्यैर्दिवाकरः ॥ 1.116.100
1.116.m: Not with jewels, nor with heaps of riches, nor with flowers and unguents / is the Sun, the lord of the universe, to be worshipped by those devoid of faith.

1.116.s:
bāhyārthanirapekṣaiśca manasaiva manogatiḥ .
niḥsvairārādhyate devo bhānuḥ sarveśvareśvaraḥ . . 101
1.116.d:
बाह्यार्थनिरपेक्षैश्च मनसैव मनोगतिः ।
निःस्वैराराध्यते देवो भानुः सर्वेश्वरेश्वरः ॥ 101
1.116.m: Indifferent to external objects, the refuge of thought is worshipped solely with the mind / by the destitute—the god Sun, ruler over all rulers.

1.116.s:
sarvametanmayā jñātaṃ yattvamāttha mahāmune .
yacca pṛcchāmi tanme tvaṃ prasādasumukho vada . . 102
1.116.d:
सर्वमेतन्मया ज्ञातं यत्त्वमात्थ महामुने ।
यच्च पृच्छामि तन्मे त्वं प्रसादसुमुखो वद ॥ 102
1.116.m: All this spoken by you, O great sage, has been understood by me. / And what I ask, speak that to me with a face gracious with favor:

1.116.s:
kathamārādhito devo naraiḥ strībhiśca bhāskaraḥ .
toṣamāyāti viprendra tadvadasva mahāmune . . 103
1.116.d:
कथमाराधितो देवो नरैः स्त्रीभिश्च भास्करः ।
तोषमायाति विप्रेन्द्र तद्वदस्व महामुने ॥ 103
1.116.m: How, when worshipped by men and by women, does the god Sun / attain satisfaction, O foremost of Brahmins? Tell that, O great sage!

1.116.s:
rahasyāni ca devasya prītaye yā tithiḥ sadā .
cānyaśeṣāṇi me brūhi arkārādhanakāṃkṣiṇaḥ . . 104
1.116.d:
रहस्यानि च देवस्य प्रीतये या तिथिः सदा ।
चान्यशेषाणि मे ब्रूहि अर्काराधनकांक्षिणः ॥ 104
1.116.m: Tell me, who desire to worship the Sun, the secrets and the lunar day that is always / pleasing to the god, and all the rest.

1.116.s:
parāvasuruvāca
śṛṇu bhūpāla yairbhānurgṛheṣyārādhyate janaiḥ .
nārībhiścātighore'sminpatitābhirbhavārṇave . . 105
1.116.d:
परावसुरुवाच
शृणु भूपाल यैर्भानुर्गृहेष्याराध्यते जनैः ।
नारीभिश्चातिघोरेऽस्मिन्पतिताभिर्भवार्णवे ॥ 105
1.116.m:
Parāvasu said:
Listen, O king, to how the Sun is worshipped in homes by people / and by women fallen into this most dreadful ocean of worldly existence.

1.116.s:
samabhyarcya jagannāthaṃ devamakaṃ samādhinā .
ekamaśnāti yo bhaktaṃ dvitīyaṃ brāhmaṇārpaṇam . . 106
1.116.d:
समभ्यर्च्य जगन्नाथं देवमकं समाधिना ।
एकमश्नाति यो भक्तं द्वितीयं ब्राह्मणार्पणम् ॥ 106
1.116.m: Having worshipped the Sun, the lord of the universe, with mental concentration, / whoever eats one meal and offers a second to a Brahmin,

1.116.s:
karoti bhāskaraprītyai kārttikaṃ māsamātmanā .
pūrve vayasi yatnena jānatā'jānatāpi vā . . 107
1.116.d:
करोति भास्करप्रीत्यै कार्त्तिकं मासमात्मना ।
पूर्वे वयसि यत्नेन जानताऽजानतापि वा ॥ 107
1.116.m: and personally performs [this] for the month of Kārttika for the pleasure of the Sun, / whatever sin was committed with effort in early life, knowingly or unknowingly,

1.116.s:
pāpamācaritaṃ tasmādbhidyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .
anenaiva vidhānena māsi mārgaśire punaḥ . . 108
1.116.d:
पापमाचरितं तस्माद्भिद्यते नात्र संशयः ।
अनेनैव विधानेन मासि मार्गशिरे पुनः ॥ 108
1.116.m: is torn away from him; there is no doubt in this. / Again, by this very same method in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa,

1.116.s:
samabhyarcya marakataṃ viprebhyo yaḥ prayacchati .
bhagavatprīṇanārthāya phalaṃ tasya śṛṇuṣva me . . 109
1.116.d:
समभ्यर्च्य मरकतं विप्रेभ्यो यः प्रयच्छति ।
भगवत्प्रीणनार्थाय फलं तस्य शृणुष्व मे ॥ 109
1.116.m: having worshipped, whoever gives emerald to the Brahmins / for the sake of pleasing the Blessed One—hear from me the fruit of that!

1.116.s:
madhye vayasi yatpāpaṃ yoṣitā puruṣeṇa vā .
kṛtamasmācca tenekto vimokṣaḥ paramātmanā . . 1.116.110
1.116.d:
मध्ये वयसि यत्पापं योषिता पुरुषेण वा ।
कृतमस्माच्च तेनेक्तो विमोक्षः परमात्मना ॥ 1.116.110
1.116.m: Whatever sin was committed in middle age by a woman or a man, / release from it is proclaimed by the Supreme Self.

1.116.s:
tathā caivekabhaktaṃ tu yastu viprāya yacchati .
divākaraṃ samabhyarcya pauṣe māsi mahīpate . . 111
1.116.d:
तथा चैवेकभक्तं तु यस्तु विप्राय यच्छति ।
दिवाकरं समभ्यर्च्य पौषे मासि महीपते ॥ 111
1.116.m: And likewise, whoever gives a single meal to a Brahmin / after worshipping the Sun in the month of Pauṣa, O ruler of the earth,

1.116.s:
tattacca prīṇayatyarkaṃ vārdhikenaiva yatkṛtam .
sa tasmānmucyate rājanpumānyoṣidathāpi vā . . 112
1.116.d:
तत्तच्च प्रीणयत्यर्कं वार्धिकेनैव यत्कृतम् ।
स तस्मान्मुच्यते राजन्पुमान्योषिदथापि वा ॥ 112
1.116.m: pleases the Sun in each case; whatever was committed in old age, / from that he is freed, O king, whether a man or a woman.

1.116.s:
trimāsikaṃ vratamidaṃ yaḥ karoti nareśvara .
sa bhānuprīṇanātpāpairlaghubhiḥ parimucyate . . 113
1.116.d:
त्रिमासिकं व्रतमिदं यः करोति नरेश्वर ।
स भानुप्रीणनात्पापैर्लघुभिः परिमुच्यते ॥ 113
1.116.m: Whoever performs this three-month observance, O lord of men, / is thoroughly freed from minor sins through pleasing the Sun.

1.116.s:
dvitīye vatsare rājanmucyate copapātakaiḥ .
tadvattṛtīye'pi kṛtaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam . . 114
1.116.d:
द्वितीये वत्सरे राजन्मुच्यते चोपपातकैः ।
तद्वत्तृतीयेऽपि कृतं महापातकनाशनम् ॥ 114
1.116.m: In the second year, O king, one is freed from secondary sins; / likewise, performed in the third [year], it destroys major sins.

1.116.s:
vratametannaraiḥ strībhistribhirmāsairanuṣṭhitam .
tribhiḥ saṃvatsaraiścaiva pradadāti phalaṃ nṛṇām . . 115
1.116.d:
व्रतमेतन्नरैः स्त्रीभिस्त्रिभिर्मासैरनुष्ठितम् ।
त्रिभिः संवत्सरैश्चैव प्रददाति फलं नृणाम् ॥ 115
1.116.m: This observance, undertaken for three months by men and women, / and likewise for three years, bestows fruit upon humans.

1.116.s:
tribhirmāsairanuṣṭhānāttrividhātpātakānnṛpa .
trīṇi nāmāni devasya mocayanti ca vārṣikaiḥ . . 116
1.116.d:
त्रिभिर्मासैरनुष्ठानात्त्रिविधात्पातकान्नृप ।
त्रीणि नामानि देवस्य मोचयन्ति च वार्षिकैः ॥ 116
1.116.m: By practice for three months, O king, from the three kinds of sins, / and three names of the god bring release through annual [observances].

1.116.s:
yatastato vratamidaṃ vividhaṃ samudāhṛtam .
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ bhāskarārādhane param . . 117
1.116.d:
यतस्ततो व्रतमिदं विविधं समुदाहृतम् ।
सर्वपापप्रशमनं भास्कराराधने परम् ॥ 117
1.116.m: Therefore, this manifold observance has been described; / it is the best [means] in the worship of the Sun for pacifying all sins.

1.116.s:
satrājita uvāca
katamāya 'tu viprāya dātavyaṃ bhaktito mune .
dvitīye dvijaśārdūla kathayasvākhilaṃ mama . . 118
1.116.d:
सत्राजित उवाच
कतमाय ऽतु विप्राय दातव्यं भक्तितो मुने ।
द्वितीये द्विजशार्दूल कथयस्वाखिलं मम ॥ 118
1.116.m:
Satrājita said:
To what kind of Brahmin should a gift be given with devotion, O sage? / On the second, O tiger among the twice-born, tell me everything!

1.116.s:
parāvasuruvāca
deye purāṇaviduṣe vastre viprottamāya ca .
śrūyatāṃ cāpi vacanaṃ yaduktaṃ bhāskareṇa ca . .
aruṇāya mahābāho pṛcchate yatpurā nṛpa . . 119
1.116.d:
परावसुरुवाच
देये पुराणविदुषे वस्त्रे विप्रोत्तमाय च ।
श्रूयतां चापि वचनं यदुक्तं भास्करेण च ॥
अरुणाय महाबाहो पृच्छते यत्पुरा नृप ॥ 119
1.116.m:
Parāvasu said:
Two garments are to be given to an excellent Brahmin who knows the Purāṇas. / And hear also the word that was spoken by the Sun / to Aruṇa, O mighty-armed king, when he asked formerly.

1.116.s:
udayācalamārūḍhaṃ bhāskaraṃ timirāpaham .
praṇamya śirasā nūnamidaṃ vacanamabravīt . . 1.116.120
1.116.d:
उदयाचलमारूढं भास्करं तिमिरापहम् ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा नूनमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 1.116.120
1.116.m: Having bowed with his head to the Sun who had mounted the mountain of sunrise, the dispeller of darkness, / he certainly spoke these words:

1.116.s:
kāni priyāṇi te deva pūjane santi sarvadā .
puṣpādīnāṃ samastānāmārādhanavidhau sadā . .
uparāgādivastrādau brāhmaṇānāṃ tathā rave . . 121
1.116.d:
कानि प्रियाणि ते देव पूजने सन्ति सर्वदा ।
पुष्पादीनां समस्तानामाराधनविधौ सदा ॥
उपरागादिवस्त्रादौ ब्राह्मणानां तथा रवे ॥ 121
1.116.m: "Which of all the flowers and other things are always pleasing to you, O god, in worship, / always in the rule of worship? / And on eclipses and the like, regarding clothing and Brahmins, O Sun?"

1.116.s:
bhāskara uvāca
puṣpāṇāṃ karavīrāṇi tathā raktaṃ ca candanam .
guggulañcāpi dhūpānāṃ naivedye modakāḥ priyāḥ . . 122
1.116.d:
भास्कर उवाच
पुष्पाणां करवीराणि तथा रक्तं च चन्दनम् ।
गुग्गुलञ्चापि धूपानां नैवेद्ये मोदकाः प्रियाः ॥ 122
1.116.m:
The Sun said:
"Among flowers, oleanders and red sandalwood, / and bdellium among incenses, and modakas as food offering are pleasing [to me].

1.116.s:
pūjākaro bhojakastu ghṛtadīpastathā priyaḥ .
dānaṃ priyaṃ khagaśreṣṭha vācakāya pradīyate . . 123
1.116.d:
पूजाकरो भोजकस्तु घृतदीपस्तथा प्रियः ।
दानं प्रियं खगश्रेष्ठ वाचकाय प्रदीयते ॥ 123
1.116.m: A Bhojaka priest who performs worship and a ghee lamp are dear, / and dear is the gift, O best of birds, that is given to a reciter.

1.116.s:
māmuddiśya ca yaddānaṃ dīyate mānavairbhuvi .
vācakāya1 tu dātavyaṃ tanmama prītaye khaga . . 124
1.116.d:
मामुद्दिश्य च यद्दानं दीयते मानवैर्भुवि ।
वाचकाय1 तु दातव्यं तन्मम प्रीतये खग ॥ 124
1.116.m: Whatever gift is given by humans on earth with me in mind / should be given to a reciter, O bird, for my pleasure.

1.116.s:
itihāsapurāṇāmyāmabhijño yastu vācakaḥ .
brāhmaṇo vai khagaśreṣṭha sampūjyaḥ prītaye mama . . 125
1.116.d:
इतिहासपुराणाम्यामभिज्ञो यस्तु वाचकः ।
ब्राह्मणो वै खगश्रेष्ठ सम्पूज्यः प्रीतये मम ॥ 125
1.116.m: A reciter who is learned in the histories and Purāṇas, / a Brahmin indeed, O best of birds, is to be worshipped for my pleasure.

1.116.s:
pūjite'sminsadā vipre pūjitohaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .
bhavāmi khagaśārdūla yatastviṣṭaḥ sa me sadā . . 126
1.116.d:
पूजितेऽस्मिन्सदा विप्रे पूजितोहं न संशयः ।
भवामि खगशार्दूल यतस्त्विष्टः स मे सदा ॥ 126
1.116.m: When this Brahmin is always worshipped, I am worshipped; there is no doubt, / O tiger among birds, because he is always dear to me.

1.116.s:
vedavīṇāmṛdaṅgaiśca nātigandhavilepanaiḥ .
tathā me jāyate prītiryathā śrutvā khagottama . . 127
1.116.d:
वेदवीणामृदङ्गैश्च नातिगन्धविलेपनैः ।
तथा मे जायते प्रीतिर्यथा श्रुत्वा खगोत्तम ॥ 127
1.116.m: Not by Vedic chanting, lutes, and drums, nor by intense fragrant ointments / does such joy arise in me, O best of birds, as upon hearing

1.116.s:
itihāsapurāṇāni vācyamānāni vācakaiḥ .
ataḥ priyo vācako me pūjākartā ca bhojakaḥ . . 128
upalepanasnāpanamāhātmyavarṇanam
1.116.d:
इतिहासपुराणानि वाच्यमानानि वाचकैः ।
अतः प्रियो वाचको मे पूजाकर्ता च भोजकः ॥ 128
उपलेपनस्नापनमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्
1.116.m:
histories and Purāṇas being recited by reciters; / therefore, dear to me is the reciter and the Bhojaka who performs the worship."
Description of the Greatness of Anointing and Bathing [the Deity]

1.117.s:
aruṇa uvāca
kimarthaṃ bhojakastubhyaṃ priyo deveśa kathyatām .
nānye viprādayo varṇā devatāyataneṣu vai . . 1
1.117.d:
अरुण उवाच
किमर्थं भोजकस्तुभ्यं प्रियो देवेश कथ्यताम् ।
नान्ये विप्रादयो वर्णा देवतायतनेषु वै ॥ 1
1.117.m:
Aruṇa said:
Why is the Bhojaka dear to you, Lord of gods? Tell me.
Why not the other classes, such as brāhmaṇas, in the temples of the deity?

1.117.s:
kaścāyaṃ bhojako deva kasya putraḥ kimātmakaḥ .
varṇataścāsya me brūhi karma cāsya samantataḥ . . 2
1.117.d:
कश्चायं भोजको देव कस्य पुत्रः किमात्मकः ।
वर्णतश्चास्य मे ब्रूहि कर्म चास्य समन्ततः ॥ 2
1.117.m: And who is this Bhojaka, O Lord? Whose son is he? What is his nature? / Tell me also of his class, and of his duty in every respect.

1.117.s:
āditya uvāca
sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi bhadraṃ te vainateya mahāmate .
śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ sarvaṃ gadato mama khecara . . 3
1.117.d:
आदित्य उवाच
साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि भद्रं ते वैनतेय महामते ।
शृणुष्वैकमनाः सर्वं गदतो मम खेचर ॥ 3
1.117.m:
Āditya said:
You have asked well, may it be well with you, wise son of Vinatā. / Listen with single-minded devotion to all that I speak, O sky-wanderer.

1.117.s:
viprādayastu ye tvanye varṇāḥ kaśyapanandana .
te pūjayanti māṃ nityaṃ bhaktiśraddhāsamanvitāḥ . .4
1.117.d:
विप्रादयस्तु ये त्वन्ये वर्णाः कश्यपनन्दन ।
ते पूजयन्ति मां नित्यं भक्तिश्रद्धासमन्विताः ॥4
1.117.m: The other classes, such as brāhmaṇas, son of Kaśyapa, / always worship me endowed with devotion and faith.

1.117.s:
devālayeṣu ye viprāḥ prītyā māṃ pūjayanti hi .
anyāśca devatāvṛttyā te syurdevalakāḥ khaga . .
etasmātkāraṇānmahyaṃ bhojako dayitaḥ sadā . . 5
1.117.d:
देवालयेषु ये विप्राः प्रीत्या मां पूजयन्ति हि ।
अन्याश्च देवतावृत्त्या ते स्युर्देवलकाः खग ॥
एतस्मात्कारणान्मह्यं भोजको दयितः सदा ॥ 5
1.117.m: Those brāhmaṇas who worship me with love in temples, / and [worship] other deities by way of livelihood, become temple-priests (devalakas), O bird. / For this reason, the Bhojaka is always dear to me.

1.117.s:
varṇato brāhmaṇaścāyaṃ svānuṣṭhānaparo yadi .
anuṣṭhānavihīno hi narakaṃ yātyasaṃśayam . . 6
1.117.d:
वर्णतो ब्राह्मणश्चायं स्वानुष्ठानपरो यदि ।
अनुष्ठानविहीनो हि नरकं यात्यसंशयम् ॥ 6
1.117.m: In terms of class he is a brāhmaṇa, if he is devoted to his proper observances. / For, devoid of proper observance, he goes to hell without doubt.

1.117.s:
na tyājyaṃ bhojakaistasmātsvakaṃ karma kadācana .
mayāsau nirmitaḥ pūrvaṃ tejasā svena vai khaga . . 7
1.117.d:
न त्याज्यं भोजकैस्तस्मात्स्वकं कर्म कदाचन ।
मयासौ निर्मितः पूर्वं तेजसा स्वेन वै खग ॥ 7
1.117.m: Therefore, his own duty must never be abandoned by a Bhojaka. / He was created by me of old through my own brilliance, O bird.

1.117.s:
pūjārthamātmano nūnaṃ karma cāsya prakīrtitam .
priyavratasuto rājā śākadvīpe mahāmatiḥ . . 8
1.117.d:
पूजार्थमात्मनो नूनं कर्म चास्य प्रकीर्तितम् ।
प्रियव्रतसुतो राजा शाकद्वीपे महामतिः ॥ 8
1.117.m: Truly his duty has been proclaimed for the sake of my worship. / There was a wise king, the son of Priyavrata, in Śākadvīpa.

1.117.s:
tena me kāritaṃ divyaṃ vimānapratimaṃ gṛham .
tasmindvīpe tadātmīye divyaṃ śilāmayaṃ mahat . . 9
1.117.d:
तेन मे कारितं दिव्यं विमानप्रतिमं गृहम् ।
तस्मिन्द्वीपे तदात्मीये दिव्यं शिलामयं महत् ॥ 9
1.117.m: By him was caused to be built for me a celestial abode resembling a celestial chariot, / a great celestial [temple] made of stone, in that continent of his.

1.117.s:
sa madarcāṃ kārayitvā kāñcanīṃ lakṣaṇānvitām .
pratiṣṭhāpanāya vai tasyāścintayāmāsa suvrataḥ . . 1.117.10
1.117.d:
स मदर्चां कारयित्वा काञ्चनीं लक्षणान्विताम् ।
प्रतिष्ठापनाय वै तस्याश्चिन्तयामास सुव्रतः ॥ 1.117.10
1.117.m: Having had an image of me made of gold, endowed with auspicious marks, / that man of good vows considered how to consecrate it:

1.117.s:
kṛtamāyatanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ teneyaṃ pratimā kṛtā .
ko vai pratiṣṭhāpayitā devamarkaṃ śubhālaye . . 11
1.117.d:
कृतमायतनं श्रेष्ठं तेनेयं प्रतिमा कृता ।
को वै प्रतिष्ठापयिता देवमर्कं शुभालये ॥ 11
1.117.m: 'An excellent temple has been made; by him this image has been made. / Who indeed will consecrate the god, the Sun, in the auspicious temple?'

1.117.s:
evaṃ sañcintayitvā tu jagāma śaraṇaṃ mama .
bhaktiṃ tasya ca sañcintya khagāhaṃ pārthivasya tu . . 12
1.117.d:
एवं सञ्चिन्तयित्वा तु जगाम शरणं मम ।
भक्तिं तस्य च सञ्चिन्त्य खगाहं पार्थिवस्य तु ॥ 12
1.117.m: Having reflected thus, he took refuge in me. / And considering the devotion of that king, O bird,

1.117.s:
gato'haṃ darśanaṃ tasya uktañcāpi mayā khaga .
kiṃ cintayasi rājendra kutaściṃtā samāgatā . . 13
1.117.d:
गतोऽहं दर्शनं तस्य उक्तञ्चापि मया खग ।
किं चिन्तयसि राजेन्द्र कुतश्चिंता समागता ॥ 13
1.117.m: I appeared before him, and I spoke, O bird: / 'What are you pondering, King of kings? Whence has this anxiety arisen?

1.117.s:
brūhi yatte hṛdi prauḍhaṃ cintākāraṇamāgatam .
saṃpādayiṣye tatsarvaṃ vimanā bhava mā nṛpa . . 14
1.117.d:
ब्रूहि यत्ते हृदि प्रौढं चिन्ताकारणमागतम् ।
संपादयिष्ये तत्सर्वं विमना भव मा नृप ॥ 14
1.117.m: Speak what is deeply rooted in your heart, the cause of worry that has come. / I shall accomplish all of it; do not be despondent, O king.

1.117.s:
atyarthaṃ duṣkaramapi kariṣye nātra saṃśayaḥ .
ityuktaḥ sa mayā rājā idaṃ vacanamabravīt . . 15
1.117.d:
अत्यर्थं दुष्करमपि करिष्ये नात्र संशयः ।
इत्युक्तः स मया राजा इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 15
1.117.m: Even if it is exceedingly difficult, I shall do it; there is no doubt of this.' / Addressed thus by me, the king spoke this word:

1.117.s:
dvīpe'smindevadevasya kṛtamāyatanaṃ tava .
mayā bhaktyā jagannātha tatheyaṃ pratimā kṛtā . . 16
1.117.d:
द्वीपेऽस्मिन्देवदेवस्य कृतमायतनं तव ।
मया भक्त्या जगन्नाथ तथेयं प्रतिमा कृता ॥ 16
1.117.m: 'A temple for you, the God of gods, has been made in this continent / by me with devotion, Lord of the world, and likewise this image has been made.

1.117.s:
pratiṣṭhāṃ kārayedyastu tava devālaye khaga .
yatra santi trayo varṇā dvīpesminkṣatriyādayaḥ . . 17
1.117.d:
प्रतिष्ठां कारयेद्यस्तु तव देवालये खग ।
यत्र सन्ति त्रयो वर्णा द्वीपेस्मिन्क्षत्रियादयः ॥ 17
1.117.m: As for one who might perform the consecration in your temple, O bird— / where three classes exist in this continent, the kṣatriyas and the rest,

1.117.s:
te mayoktā na kurvanti pratiṣṭhāṃ tava kṛtsnaśaḥ .
na cāpyarcāṃ jagannātha brāhmaṇaścātra vidyate . . 18
1.117.d:
ते मयोक्ता न कुर्वन्ति प्रतिष्ठां तव कृत्स्नशः ।
न चाप्यर्चां जगन्नाथ ब्राह्मणश्चात्र विद्यते ॥ 18
1.117.m: they, though addressed by me, do not perform your consecration in its entirety, / nor worship [it], Lord of the world; and no brāhmaṇa is found here.

1.117.s:
teneyamāgatā cintā hṛdi śalyaṃ tayārpitam .
tato mayokto rājā'sau vainateya vacaḥ śubham . . 19
1.117.d:
तेनेयमागता चिन्ता हृदि शल्यं तयार्पितम् ।
ततो मयोक्तो राजाऽसौ वैनतेय वचः शुभम् ॥ 19
1.117.m: Therefore this anxiety has come, planted like a dart in my heart.' / Then that king was addressed by me with auspicious words, O son of Vinatā:

1.117.s:
evametanna saṃdeho yathāttha tvaṃ narādhipaḥ .
kṣatriyāditrayo varṇā dvīpe'sminnātra saṃśayaḥ . . 1.117.20
1.117.d:
एवमेतन्न संदेहो यथात्थ त्वं नराधिपः ।
क्षत्रियादित्रयो वर्णा द्वीपेऽस्मिन्नात्र संशयः ॥ 1.117.20
1.117.m: 'It is so, there is no doubt, just as you say, ruler of men; / the three classes beginning with kṣatriyas [reside] in this continent, there is no doubt of this.

1.117.s:
te ca nārhanti me pūjāṃ na pratiṣṭhāṃ kadācana .
tasmātte śreyase rājanpratiṣṭhāmātmanastathā . . 21
1.117.d:
ते च नार्हन्ति मे पूजां न प्रतिष्ठां कदाचन ।
तस्मात्ते श्रेयसे राजन्प्रतिष्ठामात्मनस्तथा ॥ 21
1.117.m: And they are not entitled to my worship, nor ever to the consecration. / Therefore, for your welfare, O king, and for my own consecration,

1.117.s:
sṛjāmi prathamaṃ varṇaṃ bhaga(maga?)saṃjñamanaupamam .
ityuktvā tamahaṃ vīra rājānaṃ khagasattama . . 22
1.117.d:
सृजामि प्रथमं वर्णं भग(मग?)संज्ञमनौपमम् ।
इत्युक्त्वा तमहं वीर राजानं खगसत्तम ॥ 22
1.117.m: I create the first class, peerless, known as Maga.' / Having spoken thus to that heroic king, best of birds,

1.117.s:
jagāma paramāṃ cintāṃ tasya kāryasya siddhaye .
atha me cintayānasya1 svaśarīrādviniḥsṛtāḥ . . 23
1.117.d:
जगाम परमां चिन्तां तस्य कार्यस्य सिद्धये ।
अथ मे चिन्तयानस्य1 स्वशरीराद्विनिःसृताः ॥ 23
1.117.m: I entered into deep contemplation for the accomplishment of that purpose. / Then, as I was meditating, there came forth from my own body

1.117.s:
śaśikundendusaṃkāśāḥ saṃkhyayāṣṭau mahābalāḥ .
paṭhanti caturo vedānsāṃgopaniṣadaḥ khaga . . 24
1.117.d:
शशिकुन्देन्दुसंकाशाः संख्ययाष्टौ महाबलाः ।
पठन्ति चतुरो वेदान्सांगोपनिषदः खग ॥ 24
1.117.m: eight [men] of great strength, resembling the moon and the kunda flower, in number, / who recited the four Vedas together with their auxiliary limbs and Upaniṣads, O bird,

1.117.s:
kāṣāyavāsasaḥ sarve karaṇḍāmbujadhāriṇaḥ .
lalāṭaphalakāddvau tu dvau cānyau vakṣasastathā . . 25
1.117.d:
काषायवाससः सर्वे करण्डाम्बुजधारिणः ।
ललाटफलकाद्द्वौ तु द्वौ चान्यौ वक्षसस्तथा ॥ 25
1.117.m: all wearing ochre robes and holding reed baskets and lotuses. / Two [issued] from the surface of my forehead, and two others from my chest,

1.117.s:
caraṇābhyāṃ tathā dvau tu pādābhyāṃ dvau tathā khaga .
atha te ca mahātmānaḥ sarve praṇatakandharāḥ . . 26
1.117.d:
चरणाभ्यां तथा द्वौ तु पादाभ्यां द्वौ तथा खग ।
अथ ते च महात्मानः सर्वे प्रणतकन्धराः ॥ 26
1.117.m: two from my thighs, and two from my feet, O bird. / Then those great-souled ones, all with bowed necks,

1.117.s:
pitaraṃ manyamānā māmidaṃ vacanamabruvan .
tāta tāta mahādeva lokanātha jagatpate . . 27
1.117.d:
पितरं मन्यमाना मामिदं वचनमब्रुवन् ।
तात तात महादेव लोकनाथ जगत्पते ॥ 27
1.117.m: regarding me as their father, spoke these words: / 'Father, father, great god, Lord of the world, master of the universe,

1.117.s:
kimarthaṃ bhavatā sṛṣṭā vayaṃ devasya dehataḥ .
brūhi sarvaṃ kariṣyāma ādeśaṃ bhavato'khilam . . 28
1.117.d:
किमर्थं भवता सृष्टा वयं देवस्य देहतः ।
ब्रूहि सर्वं करिष्याम आदेशं भवतोऽखिलम् ॥ 28
1.117.m: for what purpose have we been created by you from the god's body? / Speak! We shall execute all, your entire command.

1.117.s:
pitāsmākaṃ bhavāndevo vayaṃ putrā na saṃśayaḥ .
ityuktavantaste sarve mayoktā devasambhavāḥ . . 29
1.117.d:
पितास्माकं भवान्देवो वयं पुत्रा न संशयः ।
इत्युक्तवन्तस्ते सर्वे मयोक्ता देवसम्भवाः ॥ 29
1.117.m: You, the god, are our father; we are your sons, without doubt.' / When they had spoken thus, all those born of the deity were addressed by me:

1.117.s:
priyavratasuto yoyamasya vākyaṃ kariṣyatha .
sa cāpyukto mayā rājā śākadvīpādhipaḥ khaga . . 1.117.30
1.117.d:
प्रियव्रतसुतो योयमस्य वाक्यं करिष्यथ ।
स चाप्युक्तो मया राजा शाकद्वीपाधिपः खग ॥ 1.117.30
1.117.m: 'You shall carry out the word of this king, who is the son of Priyavrata.' / And that king, ruler of Śākadvīpa, was also addressed by me, O bird:

1.117.s:
ya ete matsutā rājannarghyā brāhmaṇasattamāḥ .
kārayantu pratiṣṭhāṃ me sarvairebhirmahīpate . . 31.
kārayitvā pratiṣṭhāṃ tu mamārcāyāṃ narādhipa .
paścādāyatanaṃ sarvameṣāmarpaya pūjane . . 32
1.117.d:
य एते मत्सुता राजन्नर्घ्या ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः ।
कारयन्तु प्रतिष्ठां मे सर्वैरेभिर्महीपते ॥ 31.
कारयित्वा प्रतिष्ठां तु ममार्चायां नराधिप ।
पश्चादायतनं सर्वमेषामर्पय पूजने ॥ 32
1.117.m: 'These who are my sons, O king, venerable and best of brāhmaṇas, / let them perform my consecration, with all of them [working together], ruler of the earth. / Having had the consecration of my image performed, O ruler of men, / afterward consign the entire temple to them for worship.

1.117.s:
ete matpūjane yogyāḥ pratiṣṭhāsu ca sarvaśaḥ .
samāpya na prahartavyaṃ bhojakebhyaḥ kadācana . . 33
1.117.d:
एते मत्पूजने योग्याः प्रतिष्ठासु च सर्वशः ।
समाप्य न प्रहर्तव्यं भोजकेभ्यः कदाचन ॥ 33
1.117.m: They are fit for my worship and for consecrations in every respect. / Having completed it, one must never take [it] away from the Bhojakas.

1.117.s:
sarvamāyatanārthaṃ tu gṛhakṣetrādikaṃ ca yat .
dhanadhānyādikaṃ rājanyanmamāyatane bhavet . . 34
1.117.d:
सर्वमायतनार्थं तु गृहक्षेत्रादिकं च यत् ।
धनधान्यादिकं राजन्यन्ममायतने भवेत् ॥ 34
1.117.m: All that is for the sake of the temple—houses, fields, and the like, / and wealth, grain, and the like, O king, which may belong to my temple—

1.117.s:
tatsarvaṃ bhojakebhyastu dātavyaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ .
dhanadhānyasuvarṇādi gṛhakṣetrādikaṃ ca yat . .
yanmadīyaṃ bhavetkiñjidgrāme vā nagare kvacit . . 35
1.117.d:
तत्सर्वं भोजकेभ्यस्तु दातव्यं नात्र संशयः ।
धनधान्यसुवर्णादि गृहक्षेत्रादिकं च यत् ॥
यन्मदीयं भवेत्किञ्जिद्ग्रामे वा नगरे क्वचित् ॥ 35
1.117.m: all that must be given to the Bhojakas, without doubt. / Wealth, grain, gold, and the like, houses, fields, and the like, / whatever may be mine in a village or anywhere in a city,

1.117.s:
tasya sarvasya rājendra madīyasya samantataḥ .
adhipā bhojakāḥ sarve nānye viprādayo nṛpa . . 36
1.117.d:
तस्य सर्वस्य राजेन्द्र मदीयस्य समन्ततः ।
अधिपा भोजकाः सर्वे नान्ये विप्रादयो नृप ॥ 36
1.117.m: of all that which is mine on every side, King of kings, / the Bhojakas are all the masters, not the other [classes] such as brāhmaṇas, O king.

1.117.s:
yathādhikārī putrastu pitṛdravyasya vai bhavet .
tathā madīyavittasya bhojakāḥ syurna saṃśayaḥ . . 37
1.117.d:
यथाधिकारी पुत्रस्तु पितृद्रव्यस्य वै भवेत् ।
तथा मदीयवित्तस्य भोजकाः स्युर्न संशयः ॥ 37
1.117.m: Just as a son would be the rightful owner of his father's property, / so the Bhojakas should be [the owners] of my property, without doubt.'

1.117.s:
ityuktena mayā rājñā tathā sarvaṃ pravartitam .
kārayitvā pratiṣṭhāṃ tu dattvā sarvasvameva hi . .
bhojakebhyaḥ khagaśreṣṭha tato harṣamavāptavān . . 38
1.117.d:
इत्युक्तेन मया राज्ञा तथा सर्वं प्रवर्तितम् ।
कारयित्वा प्रतिष्ठां तु दत्त्वा सर्वस्वमेव हि ॥
भोजकेभ्यः खगश्रेष्ठ ततो हर्षमवाप्तवान् ॥ 38
1.117.m: Being addressed thus by me, everything was carried out accordingly by the king. / Having had the consecration performed and having given all his possessions indeed / to the Bhojakas, O best of birds, he then attained joy.

1.117.s:
evamete mayā sṛṣṭā bhojakā garuḍāgraja .
ahamātmā tato hyeṣāṃ sarve sumanasastathā . . 39
1.117.d:
एवमेते मया सृष्टा भोजका गरुडाग्रज ।
अहमात्मा ततो ह्येषां सर्वे सुमनसस्तथा ॥ 39
1.117.m: Thus were these Bhojakas created by me, elder brother of Garuḍa. / Therefore I am their self, and they are all of good mind.

1.117.s:
matputreṇa samā jñeyāstathā mama hitāḥ sadā .
tasmāttebhyaḥ pradātavyaṃ na hartavyaṃ kadācana . . 1.117.40
1.117.d:
मत्पुत्रेण समा ज्ञेयास्तथा मम हिताः सदा ।
तस्मात्तेभ्यः प्रदातव्यं न हर्तव्यं कदाचन ॥ 1.117.40
1.117.m: They are to be known as equal to my sons, and always devoted to my welfare. / Therefore [property] should be given to them; it should never be taken away.

1.117.s:
bhojakasya haredyastu lobhāddveṣāttathāpi vā .
sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ tāmisraṃ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ . . 41
1.117.d:
भोजकस्य हरेद्यस्तु लोभाद्द्वेषात्तथापि वा ।
स याति नरकं घोरं तामिस्रं शाश्वतीः समाः ॥ 41
1.117.m: Whoever steals from a Bhojaka out of greed or hatred, / he goes to the terrible hell of Tāmisra for eternal years.

1.117.s:
tasmādgrāmādikaṃ dravyaṃ yatkiñcinmama vidyate .
tatsarvaṃ bhojakasvaṃ hi pitṛparyāgataṃ mama . . 42
1.117.d:
तस्माद्ग्रामादिकं द्रव्यं यत्किञ्चिन्मम विद्यते ।
तत्सर्वं भोजकस्वं हि पितृपर्यागतं मम ॥ 42
1.117.m: Therefore, villages and other property, whatever little belongs to me, / all that is truly the property of the Bhojakas, handed down to me from a father.

1.117.s:
bhojakaśca bhavedyādṛktatte vacmi khageśvara .
mamājñāṃ pāleyadyastu svānuṣṭhānaparaḥ sadā . . 43
1.117.d:
भोजकश्च भवेद्यादृक्तत्ते वच्मि खगेश्वर ।
ममाज्ञां पालेयद्यस्तु स्वानुष्ठानपरः सदा ॥ 43
1.117.m: And what sort of person a Bhojaka should be, that I shall tell you, O lord of birds: / one who obeys my command and is always devoted to his proper practice;

1.117.s:
vedādhigamanaṃ pūrvaṃ dārasaṃgrahaṇaṃ tathā .
abhyaṅgadhāraṇaṃ nityaṃ tathā triṣavaṇaṃ smṛtam . . 44
1.117.d:
वेदाधिगमनं पूर्वं दारसंग्रहणं तथा ।
अभ्यङ्गधारणं नित्यं तथा त्रिषवणं स्मृतम् ॥ 44
1.117.m: first the acquisition of the Veda, and likewise the taking of a wife; / daily application of oil-massage, and likewise thrice-daily bathing is taught;

1.117.s:
pañcakṛtvaḥ sadā pūjyo hyahaṃ rātrau dine tathā .
devabrāhmaṇavedānāṃ nindā kāryā na vai kvacit . . 45
1.117.d:
पञ्चकृत्वः सदा पूज्यो ह्यहं रात्रौ दिने तथा ।
देवब्राह्मणवेदानां निन्दा कार्या न वै क्वचित् ॥ 45
1.117.m: I am always to be worshipped five times, both at night and by day; / and censure of gods, Brahmins, and the Vedas should never be uttered anywhere.

1.117.s:
nānyādevapratiṣṭhā tu kāryā vai bhojakena tu .
mamāpi ca na kartavyā tena ekākinā kvacit . . 46
1.117.d:
नान्यादेवप्रतिष्ठा तु कार्या वै भोजकेन तु ।
ममापि च न कर्तव्या तेन एकाकिना क्वचित् ॥ 46
1.117.m: No consecration of any other deity should be performed by a Bhojaka, / nor should [the consecration] even of me ever be performed by him alone.

1.117.s:
sarvameva nivedyānnaṃ nāśnīyādbhojakaḥ sadā .
na bhuñjīta gṛhaṃ gatvā śūdrasya garuḍāgraja . . 47
1.117.d:
सर्वमेव निवेद्यान्नं नाश्नीयाद्भोजकः सदा ।
न भुञ्जीत गृहं गत्वा शूद्रस्य गरुडाग्रज ॥ 47
1.117.m: A Bhojaka must never consume all the offered food; / he should not go to the house of a Śūdra and eat, O elder brother of Garuḍa.

1.117.s:
śūdrocchiṣṭaṃ prayatnena sadā tyājyaṃ hi bhojakaiḥ .
ye'śnanti bhojakā nityaṃ śūdrānnaṃ śūdraveśmani . . 48
1.117.d:
शूद्रोच्छिष्टं प्रयत्नेन सदा त्याज्यं हि भोजकैः ।
येऽश्नन्ति भोजका नित्यं शूद्रान्नं शूद्रवेश्मनि ॥ 48
1.117.m: A Śūdra's leftovers must always be avoided with diligence by Bhojakas. / Those Bhojakas who regularly eat a Śūdra's food in a Śūdra's house—

1.117.s:
te vai pūjāphalaṃ cātra kathaṃ prāpsyanti khecara .
gatvā gṛhaṃ tu śūdrasya na bhoktavyaṃ kadācana . . 49
1.117.d:
ते वै पूजाफलं चात्र कथं प्राप्स्यन्ति खेचर ।
गत्वा गृहं तु शूद्रस्य न भोक्तव्यं कदाचन ॥ 49
1.117.m: how indeed will they obtain the fruit of worship in this matter, O sky-wanderer? / Having gone to the house of a Śūdra, one must never eat.

1.117.s:
gṛhāgataṃ ca śūdrānnaṃ tacca tyājyaṃ tathaiva ca .
ādhmātavyombujo nityaṃ bhojakenāgrato mama . . 1.117.50
1.117.d:
गृहागतं च शूद्रान्नं तच्च त्याज्यं तथैव च ।
आध्मातव्योम्बुजो नित्यं भोजकेनाग्रतो मम ॥ 1.117.50
1.117.m: And a Śūdra's food brought to one's house must likewise be abandoned. / A conch must always be blown by the Bhojaka before me.

1.117.s:
sakṛtpravādite śaṃkhe mama prītirhi jāyate .
ṣaṇmāsānnātra sandehaḥ purāṇaśravaṇaṃ tathā . . 51
1.117.d:
सकृत्प्रवादिते शंखे मम प्रीतिर्हि जायते ।
षण्मासान्नात्र सन्देहः पुराणश्रवणं तथा ॥ 51
1.117.m: When the conch is sounded once, my delight is produced / for six months, without a doubt; and likewise from the hearing of a Purāṇa.

1.117.s:
tasmācchaṃkhaḥ sadā vādyo bhojakena prayatnataḥ .
tasyeyaṃ paramā vṛttirnaivedyaṃ yanmadīyakam . . 52
1.117.d:
तस्माच्छंखः सदा वाद्यो भोजकेन प्रयत्नतः ।
तस्येयं परमा वृत्तिर्नैवेद्यं यन्मदीयकम् ॥ 52
1.117.m: Therefore the conch should always be sounded with effort by the Bhojaka. / This is his supreme livelihood: that which is my food-offering.

1.117.s:
nābhojyaṃ bhuñjate yasmāttenaite bhojakā matāḥ .
magaṃ dhyāyanti te yasmāttena te magadhāḥ smṛtāḥ . . 53
1.117.d:
नाभोज्यं भुञ्जते यस्मात्तेनैते भोजका मताः ।
मगं ध्यायन्ति ते यस्मात्तेन ते मगधाः स्मृताः ॥ 53
1.117.m: Because they do not eat what is inedible, therefore they are considered Bhojakas. / Because they meditate upon Maga, therefore they are known as Magadhas.

1.117.s:
bhojayanti ca māṃ nityaṃ tena te bhojakā smṛtāḥ .
abhyaṅgaṃ ca prayatnena prāyaṃ śuddhikaraṃ param . . 54
1.117.d:
भोजयन्ति च मां नित्यं तेन ते भोजका स्मृताः ।
अभ्यङ्गं च प्रयत्नेन प्रायं शुद्धिकरं परम् ॥ 54
1.117.m: And because they feed me daily, therefore they are called Bhojakas. / And oil-massage, performed with effort, is generally the supreme purifier.

1.117.s:
abhyaṅgahīno hyaśucirbhojakaḥ syānna saṃśayaḥ .
yastu māṃ pūjayedvīra abhyaṅgena vinā khaga . . 55
1.117.d:
अभ्यङ्गहीनो ह्यशुचिर्भोजकः स्यान्न संशयः ।
यस्तु मां पूजयेद्वीर अभ्यङ्गेन विना खग ॥ 55
1.117.m: A Bhojaka devoid of oil-massage would surely be impure, without doubt. / But he who worships me without oil-massage, O hero, O bird,

1.117.s:
na tasya santatiḥ syādvai na cāhaṃ prītimānbhave1 .
muṇḍanaṃ śirasā kāryaṃ śikhā dhāryā prayatnataḥ . . 56
1.117.d:
न तस्य सन्ततिः स्याद्वै न चाहं प्रीतिमान्भवे1 ।
मुण्डनं शिरसा कार्यं शिखा धार्या प्रयत्नतः ॥ 56
1.117.m: he will have no offspring, nor will I be pleased. / Shaving of the head should be done, and a tuft of hair must be kept with care.

1.117.s:
naktaṃ cādityadivase tathā ṣaṣṭhyāṃ pravartayet .
saptamyāmupavāsastu mama saṃkramaṇe tathā . . 57
1.117.d:
नक्तं चादित्यदिवसे तथा षष्ठ्यां प्रवर्तयेत् ।
सप्तम्यामुपवासस्तु मम संक्रमणे तथा ॥ 57
1.117.m: And one should observe a nocturnal meal on Sunday, and likewise on the sixth lunar day; / but on the seventh lunar day, as well as on my transit, fasting

1.117.s:
kartavyo bhojakenaiva matprītyai garuḍāgraja .
trikālaṃ cāpi gāyatrīṃ japedvācā puro mama . . 58
1.117.d:
कर्तव्यो भोजकेनैव मत्प्रीत्यै गरुडाग्रज ।
त्रिकालं चापि गायत्रीं जपेद्वाचा पुरो मम ॥ 58
1.117.m: must be performed by the Bhojaka for my pleasure, O elder brother of Garuḍa. / And he should recite the Gāyatrī aloud before me at the three junctures of the day.

1.117.s:
mukhamāvṛtya yatnena pūjanīyo'hamādarāt .
maunaṃ cāsya prayatnena tyaktvā krodhaṃ ca dūrataḥ . . 59
1.117.d:
मुखमावृत्य यत्नेन पूजनीयोऽहमादरात् ।
मौनं चास्य प्रयत्नेन त्यक्त्वा क्रोधं च दूरतः ॥ 59
1.117.m: Covering his mouth with care, I should be worshipped with respect, / his silence [observed] with effort, casting anger far away.

1.117.s:
śūdrebhyo yastu vaiśyebhyo lobhātkāmātprayacchati .
nirmālyaṃ mama vai vatsa sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam . . 1.117.60
1.117.d:
शूद्रेभ्यो यस्तु वैश्येभ्यो लोभात्कामात्प्रयच्छति ।
निर्माल्यं मम वै वत्स स याति नरकं ध्रुवम् ॥ 1.117.60
1.117.m: He who, out of greed or desire, gives my leftover offering / to Śūdras or to Vaiśyas, O dear child, surely goes to hell.

1.117.s:
lobhādvai bhojako yastu matpuṣpāṇi khagādhipa .
yacchatenyasya duṣṭātmā mayyanāropya khecara . . 61
1.117.d:
लोभाद्वै भोजको यस्तु मत्पुष्पाणि खगाधिप ।
यच्छतेन्यस्य दुष्टात्मा मय्यनारोप्य खेचर ॥ 61
1.117.m: The evil-minded Bhojaka who, out of greed, O lord of birds, / gives my flowers to another without offering them to me, O sky-wanderer,

1.117.s:
sa jñeyo me paraḥ śatruḥ sa māmarho na cārcitum .
nirmālyaṃ mama deyaṃ syādbrāhmaṇādiṣu vai nṛṣu . . 62
1.117.d:
स ज्ञेयो मे परः शत्रुः स मामर्हो न चार्चितुम् ।
निर्माल्यं मम देयं स्याद्ब्राह्मणादिषु वै नृषु ॥ 62
1.117.m: he should be known as my supreme enemy; he is not worthy to worship me. / My leftover offering may be given to men such as Brahmins.

1.117.s:
naivedyaṃ yanmadīyaṃ tu tadaśnīyātsadaiva hi .
tenāsau śuddhyate nityaṃ haviṣyānnasamaṃ tathā . . 63
1.117.d:
नैवेद्यं यन्मदीयं तु तदश्नीयात्सदैव हि ।
तेनासौ शुद्ध्यते नित्यं हविष्यान्नसमं तथा ॥ 63
1.117.m: That which is my food-offering he should always eat; / by that he is constantly purified, as if [eating] sacrificial food.

1.117.s:
tatkṣaṇādutkṣipedyastu mamāṃgātpuṣpameva hi .
nānyasya deyaṃ naivedyaṃ madīyamudake2 kṣipet . . 64
1.117.d:
तत्क्षणादुत्क्षिपेद्यस्तु ममांगात्पुष्पमेव हि ।
नान्यस्य देयं नैवेद्यं मदीयमुदके2 क्षिपेत् ॥ 64
1.117.m: He who immediately lifts a flower from my body / should not give it to another; he should cast my food-offering into water.

1.117.s:
pañcagavyasamaṃ tasya manmataṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ .
mamāṅgalagnaṃ yatkiñcidgandhaṃ puṣpamathāpi vā . . 65
1.117.d:
पञ्चगव्यसमं तस्य मन्मतं नात्र संशयः ।
ममाङ्गलग्नं यत्किञ्चिद्गन्धं पुष्पमथापि वा ॥ 65
1.117.m: In my opinion, it is equal to the five cow-products; there is no doubt about this. / Whatever perfume or flower has touched my body

1.117.s:
dātavyaṃ na ca vaiśyāya na śūdrāya kadācana .
ātmanā tadgrahītavyaṃ na vikreyaṃ kathañcana . . 66
1.117.d:
दातव्यं न च वैश्याय न शूद्राय कदाचन ।
आत्मना तद्ग्रहीतव्यं न विक्रेयं कथञ्चन ॥ 66
1.117.m: must never be given to a Vaiśya, nor ever to a Śūdra. / It should be taken by oneself; it must not be sold in any way.

1.117.s:
yastu nāropya puṣpāṇi avyaṅgāni mamopari .
yaḥ kaścidāharelloke sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam . . 67
1.117.d:
यस्तु नारोप्य पुष्पाणि अव्यङ्गानि ममोपरि ।
यः कश्चिदाहरेल्लोके स याति नरकं ध्रुवम् ॥ 67
1.117.m: Whoever takes away without offering to me flowers / that have all their petals, whoever he may be in the world, surely goes to hell.

1.117.s:
snapanaṃ mama nirmālyaṃ pāvakaṃ yastu laṅghayet .
sa naro narakaṃ yāti saraudraṃ rauravaṃ khaga . . 68
1.117.d:
स्नपनं मम निर्माल्यं पावकं यस्तु लङ्घयेत् ।
स नरो नरकं याति सरौद्रं रौरवं खग ॥ 68
1.117.m: The man who steps over my bath-water, my leftover offering, or fire, / goes to the dreadful Raurava hell, O bird.

1.117.s:
bhojakena sadā kāryaṃ snapanaṃ me prayatnataḥ .
yathā na laṅghayetkaścidyathā śvā nāpi bhakṣayet . . 69
1.117.d:
भोजकेन सदा कार्यं स्नपनं मे प्रयत्नतः ।
यथा न लङ्घयेत्कश्चिद्यथा श्वा नापि भक्षयेत् ॥ 69
1.117.m: The Bhojaka must always carefully attend to my bath-water, / so that no one steps over it, and so that a dog does not lap it up.

1.117.s:
yadyayatnaparaḥ kuryādbhojakaḥ snapanaṃ mama .
yathā vai laṅghitamatirbhakṣyatāṃ ca khagādhipa . . 1.117.70
1.117.d:
यद्ययत्नपरः कुर्याद्भोजकः स्नपनं मम ।
यथा वै लङ्घितमतिर्भक्ष्यतां च खगाधिप ॥ 1.117.70
1.117.m: If a careless Bhojaka should dispose of my bath-water / such that it is stepped over or consumed, O lord of birds,

1.117.s:
sa yāti narakaṃ raudraṃ tāmiśraṃ nāma nāmataḥ .
ekabhaktaṃ sadā kāryaṃ snānaṃ traikālameva hi . . 71
1.117.d:
स याति नरकं रौद्रं तामिश्रं नाम नामतः ।
एकभक्तं सदा कार्यं स्नानं त्रैकालमेव हि ॥ 71
1.117.m: he goes to the terrible hell named Tāmisra. / Only one meal a day should ever be eaten, and bathing done at the three junctures.

1.117.s:
tricailaṃ parivarteta bhavitavyaṃ dinedine .
pūjākāle'rghakāle ca krodhastyājyaḥ prayatnataḥ . . 72
1.117.d:
त्रिचैलं परिवर्तेत भवितव्यं दिनेदिने ।
पूजाकालेऽर्घकाले च क्रोधस्त्याज्यः प्रयत्नतः ॥ 72
1.117.m: He should change three garments day by day. / At the time of worship and at the time of the water-offering, anger must be avoided with care.

1.117.s:
amāṃgalyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ vaktavyaṃ ca śubhaṃ tadā .
īdṛgbhūto bhojako me preyān pūjākaraḥ sadā . . 73
1.117.d:
अमांगल्यं न वक्तव्यं वक्तव्यं च शुभं तदा ।
ईदृग्भूतो भोजको मे प्रेयान् पूजाकरः सदा ॥ 73
1.117.m: Nothing inauspicious should be spoken, and auspicious words must be spoken then. / Such a Bhojaka, constantly performing my worship, is very dear to me.

1.117.s:
sanmānyaḥ pūjanīyaśca viprādīnāṃ yathāsmyaham .
yaḥ karotyavamānaṃ tu vṛttirūpaṃ tu bhojake . . 74
1.117.d:
सन्मान्यः पूजनीयश्च विप्रादीनां यथास्म्यहम् ।
यः करोत्यवमानं तु वृत्तिरूपं तु भोजके ॥ 74
1.117.m: He is to be honoured and worshipped just as I am by Brahmins and others. / But he who shows contempt toward the livelihood of a Bhojaka—

1.117.s:
tasyāhaṃ roṣametyāśu kulaṃ hanmi samantataḥ .
priyo me bhojako nityaṃ yathā tvaṃ vinatāsuta . . 75
1.117.d:
तस्याहं रोषमेत्याशु कुलं हन्मि समन्ततः ।
प्रियो मे भोजको नित्यं यथा त्वं विनतासुत ॥ 75
1.117.m: I, quickly becoming angry, destroy his family completely. / A Bhojaka is always dear to me, just as you are, O son of Vinatā,

1.117.s:
upalepanakartā ca sammārjanaparaśca yaḥ . .
parāvasuruvāca
ityuktvā bhagavānbhānurbabhrāma rathamāsthitaḥ . . 76
1.117.d:
उपलेपनकर्ता च सम्मार्जनपरश्च यः ॥
परावसुरुवाच
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्भानुर्बभ्राम रथमास्थितः ॥ 76
1.117.m: as is he who performs the smearing [of the floor] and is devoted to sweeping. / Parāvasu said: / Having spoken thus, the blessed Sun wandered, seated in his chariot.

1.117.s:
aruṇo'pi tathā śrutvā mudayā parayā nṛpaḥ .
pūjyastasmānmahārāja bhojakastu mahīpate . . 77
1.117.d:
अरुणोऽपि तथा श्रुत्वा मुदया परया नृपः ।
पूज्यस्तस्मान्महाराज भोजकस्तु महीपते ॥ 77
1.117.m: Aruṇa too, having heard thus, [was filled] with supreme joy, O king. / Therefore a Bhojaka is to be worshipped, O great king, O ruler of the earth.

1.117.s: tasmāddevaṃ vācakāya dvitīyamaśanaṃ naraiḥ . . 78
1.117.d: तस्माद्देवं वाचकाय द्वितीयमशनं नरैः ॥ 78
1.117.m: Therefore a second meal should be given to the reciter by men.

1.117.s:
brahmovāca
itthaṃ śrutvā sa rājā tu karmaṇaḥ phalamātmanaḥ .
purātanaṃ mahābāhurmudamāpa mahīpatiḥ . .79
1.117.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्थं श्रुत्वा स राजा तु कर्मणः फलमात्मनः ।
पुरातनं महाबाहुर्मुदमाप महीपतिः ॥79
1.117.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard thus of the ancient fruit of his own action, / that king, the mighty-armed ruler of the earth, experienced joy.

1.117.s:
yadyadāyatanaṃ bhānoḥ pṛthivyāṃ paśyate nṛpaḥ .
tasmiṃstasminkārayati upalepanamādarāt . . 1.117.80
1.117.d:
यद्यदायतनं भानोः पृथिव्यां पश्यते नृपः ।
तस्मिंस्तस्मिन्कारयति उपलेपनमादरात् ॥ 1.117.80
1.117.m: Whatever temple of the Sun the king saw on earth, / in each one he respectfully had the smearing [of the floor] performed.

1.117.s:
bhāryā tasyāpi suśroṇi puṇyaśravaṇamādarāt .
vācake vetanaṃ dattvā bhānordevasya mandire . . 81
1.117.d:
भार्या तस्यापि सुश्रोणि पुण्यश्रवणमादरात् ।
वाचके वेतनं दत्त्वा भानोर्देवस्य मन्दिरे ॥ 81
1.117.m: His wife too, O fair-hipped one, out of desire to hear the holy [lore] with reverence, / gave a fee to the reciter in the temple of the god Sun.

1.117.s:
itthaṃ rājā sapatnīkaḥ pūjya bhaktyā divākaram .
prāptāvubhau parāṃ prītiṃ gatiṃ cānuttamāṃ tathā . . 82
satrājitopākhyānaṃ samāptam
dīpadānaphalavarṇanam
1.117.d:
इत्थं राजा सपत्नीकः पूज्य भक्त्या दिवाकरम् ।
प्राप्तावुभौ परां प्रीतिं गतिं चानुत्तमां तथा ॥ 82
सत्राजितोपाख्यानं समाप्तम्
दीपदानफलवर्णनम्
1.117.m:
Thus the king, together with his wife, having worshipped the Sun with devotion, / both attained supreme joy and an unsurpassed realm.
The narrative of Satrājit is concluded.
Description of the Fruit of Giving Lamps.

1.118.s:
brahmovāca
dīpaṃ prayacchati naro bhānorāyatane tu yaḥ .
tejasā ravisaṃkāśaḥ sarvayajñaphalaṃ1 labhet . . 1
1.118.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
दीपं प्रयच्छति नरो भानोरायतने तु यः ।
तेजसा रविसंकाशः सर्वयज्ञफलं1 लभेत् ॥ 1
1.118.m: Brahmā said: / The man who offers a lamp in the temple of the Sun, / resplendent like the sun with splendour, obtains the fruit of all sacrifices.

1.118.s:
kārttike tu viśeṣeṇa kaumāre māsi dīpakam .
datvā phalamavāpnoti yadanyena na labhyate . . 2
1.118.d:
कार्त्तिके तु विशेषेण कौमारे मासि दीपकम् ।
दत्वा फलमवाप्नोति यदन्येन न लभ्यते ॥ 2
1.118.m: Especially in Kārttika, in the month of Kumāra, having given a lamp, / he obtains a fruit that cannot be attained by any other means.

1.118.s:
kṛṣṇakṛṣṇātra te vacmi saṃvādaṃ pāpanāśanam .
bhrātṛbhiḥ saha bhadrasya brāhmaṇasya mahātmanaḥ . . 3
1.118.d:
कृष्णकृष्णात्र ते वच्मि संवादं पापनाशनम् ।
भ्रातृभिः सह भद्रस्य ब्राह्मणस्य महात्मनः ॥ 3
1.118.m: O black-and-dark one, I shall tell you here a dialogue that destroys sin, / between the high-souled Brahmin Bhadra and his brothers.

1.118.s:
jagatyasminpurī ramyā nāmnā māhiṣmatī purā .
tasyāmāsīddvijaḥ kṛṣṇa nāgaśarmeti viśrutaḥ . .4
1.118.d:
जगत्यस्मिन्पुरी रम्या नाम्ना माहिष्मती पुरा ।
तस्यामासीद्द्विजः कृष्ण नागशर्मेति विश्रुतः ॥4
1.118.m:
In this world, in ancient times, there was a delightful city named Māhiṣmatī.
In it lived a twice-born, O Kṛṣṇa, renowned as Nāgaśarman.

1.118.s:
tasya putraśataṃ jātaṃ prasādādbhāskarasya ca .
teṣāṃ kaniṣṭho bhadrastu tatputrāṇāṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ . . 5
1.118.d:
तस्य पुत्रशतं जातं प्रसादाद्भास्करस्य च ।
तेषां कनिष्ठो भद्रस्तु तत्पुत्राणां विचक्षणः ॥ 5
1.118.m:
A hundred sons were born to him by the grace of the Sun.
Among them, the youngest of his sons was the wise Bhadra.

1.118.s:
sa ca nityaṃ jagaddhāturdevadevasya bhāsvataḥ .
dīpavartiparastadvattailādyāharaṇodyataḥ . . 6
1.118.d:
स च नित्यं जगद्धातुर्देवदेवस्य भास्वतः ।
दीपवर्तिपरस्तद्वत्तैलाद्याहरणोद्यतः ॥ 6
1.118.m:
And he was continually devoted to the lamps and wicks of the Radiant One,
the God of gods, supporter of the universe, and likewise bent on fetching oil and the rest.

1.118.s:
bhānorāyatane tasya sahasraṃ bhārgavīpriya .
pradīpānāṃ tu jajvāla divārātramaninditam . .7
1.118.d:
भानोरायतने तस्य सहस्रं भार्गवीप्रिय ।
प्रदीपानां तु जज्वाल दिवारात्रमनिन्दितम् ॥7
1.118.m:
In the temple of the Sun, O beloved of Bhārgavī,
a thousand faultless lamps burned day and night through him.

1.118.s:
tasya dīptyā parābhūtāstasya lāvaṇyadharṣitāḥ .
sarve te bhrātaro bhadraṃ papracchuridamādarāt . . 8
1.118.d:
तस्य दीप्त्या पराभूतास्तस्य लावण्यधर्षिताः ।
सर्वे ते भ्रातरो भद्रं पप्रच्छुरिदमादरात् ॥ 8
1.118.m:
Overcome by his splendour and overwhelmed by his beauty,
all those brothers questioned Bhadra with respect:

1.118.s:
bho bhadra vada vai bhrātarbhadraṃ testu sadā dvija .
kautūhalaparāḥ sarve yatpṛcchāmastaducyatām . . 9
1.118.d:
भो भद्र वद वै भ्रातर्भद्रं तेस्तु सदा द्विज ।
कौतूहलपराः सर्वे यत्पृच्छामस्तदुच्यताम् ॥ 9
1.118.m:
"O Bhadra! Speak, brother—may auspiciousness be yours always, twice-born!
Filled with curiosity, all of us ask: let that be told.

1.118.s:
teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhadro vacanamabravīt .
viṣaye sati vaktavyaṃ yanmayā tadihocyatām . . 1.118.10
1.118.d:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा भद्रो वचनमब्रवीत् ।
विषये सति वक्तव्यं यन्मया तदिहोच्यताम् ॥ 1.118.10
1.118.m:
